meta.g6_holdout_note: G6 (Oct22-Nov4) is the FIRST TRUE blind holdout scored on s95.1. Roll-adjusted, G6 was a V: week-1 give-back DOWN (3.52->3.14) then week-2 recovery UP (->3.66), net +0.14. The forecast leaned down (reversion lean) and: (a) CAUGHT the week-1 give-back DIRECTION (cross_block_reversion earned week-1); (b) MISSED the week-2 recovery - the intra-block turn / counter-trend recovery, the OPEN problem, still unsolved (same failure mode as 0916); (c) MAGNITUDE was the DOMINANT error (undersized both the dip and the recovery); (d) the storage SURPLUS (bearish) got the block direction WRONG - winter heating-demand (HDD rising) won. LESSONS FOLDED: cross_block_reversion is a GIVE-BACK, not a sustained reversal (a block can V back - as G5 and G6 both did); fundamentals are NOT even a reliable block-direction cue near the winter transition (rising HDD flips the sign); magnitude remains the dominant residual; the intra-block counter-trend turn is the top open problem.

meta.s96_2_refine_note: S96.2 UNBLINDED per-group refine of G7 (Nov5-18, first winter block) - ITERATIVE (Greg S96): refined curves written into forecasts/grp7.json (refined_* fields), derived ONLY from general rules + decision-state + prior-day ACTUAL tape (never the forecast day's own tape). NEW/CHANGED RULES (each n>=2 spanning groups): (R1) GIVE-BACK-EXHAUSTION DAY-BOUNDARY READ - new play direction.giveback_exhaustion_boundary: a give-back day that closes >=~40-50% off its intraday extreme with a last-hours counter-tick, while the underlying swing's big legs show no continuation-collapse -> give-back EXHAUSTED, swing resumes next session (1105->1106, 1107->1109 gap, 1110->1111, 1112->1113 G7; 0926->0929, 1003->1005 G4); a give-back that closes AT its extreme with last hours extending CONTINUES (1002->1003 G4, 1114->1117 G7); if the swing side's own legs already collapsed, stand down (0915 down-legs 0/8 -> the 0916 counter-grind correctly filtered). THIS is the day-level SEQUENCING answer: the carrier day (1111 not 1110) is pinned by the boundary read off day-N-1 actuals. (R2) STORAGE-THURSDAY SIDE = RUNNING SWING/TURN STATE, NEVER THE PRINT SIGN - reframed into daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude: 10 storage Thursdays across G3-G7 all sided with the swing (or the just-armed turn: 0925, 1030), zero with the surprise sign when they disagreed (1106 +1350 THROUGH +10.8-above; 1113 +620 THROUGH +5.2-above). (R3) WEEKEND-GAP DELIVERY + MONDAY GAP-REACTION - reframed into daytype.monday_weekend_gap: the weekend repricing is delivered at the SUNDAY reopen gap; Monday's US session is the REACTION: gap WITH a mature swing to a fresh extreme is FADED (1109+1560->1110 -820; 0908 mild), gap at a FRESH turn is EXTENDED (1019->1020 +2660); with no material gap Monday carries Friday's side (1107->1110, 1114->1117, 0919->0922, 1017->1020). Monday-as-block-reversal is DEAD - it was swing-state coincidence. (R4) MATURE-SWING ALTERNATION - new play structure.mature_swing_alternation: a young swing (<=3 sessions from the turn) chains extensions (0929-1001 G4; 1030-1104 G6); a mature swing (>=4 sessions) never extends a material fresh extreme close - next session is a give-back/hold (G7 5/5; 1007->1008 G4). (R5) GIVE-BACK ORIGIN-SHELF FLOOR - new play level.giveback_origin_shelf: a terminal give-back runs to the swing's origin shelf then stabilizes; at >=~75% retrace the R1 closes-at-low read INVERTS (capitulation precedes the bounce: 0922->0923, 1016->1017, 1117->1118). REFINED-vs-ACTUAL (per-event): 1105 -500/-520, 1106 +1400/+1350, 1107 -650/-720, 1110 -800/-820 (weekend gap +1200/+1560), 1111 +1400/+1580, 1112 -100/+100 (sign miss, hold-day), 1113 +800/+620, 1114 -900/-910, 1117 -1400/-1500, 1118 +250/+270. IRREDUCIBLE at the open: (a) the hold-day sign inside +-150 (1112); (b) the EXTREME magnitudes (1111 +1580 on a thin holiday - direction+size-up callable, full size not; the standing dominant residual); (c) the Sunday-gap SIZE (1109 +1560 - direction callable via R1, magnitude not); (d) the R5 bounce-day timing rests on a soft >=75%-retrace threshold (n=3). GUARD: rules were applied UNIFORMLY across the block and back-checked on G3-6; sizes come from condition-class bands (mature-swing give-back -500..-900; catalyst resume +800..+1400), never from the target day's tape.

meta.s97_2_refine_note: S97.2 UNBLINDED per-group refine of G8 (Nov19-Dec2, deep winter onset) - refined curves in forecasts/grp8.json (refined_* fields), derived ONLY from general rules + decision-state + prior-day ACTUAL tape; sizes from condition-class bands, never the target day's tape. THE HEADLINE: the whole block is ONE ALTERNATION CHAIN (extension 1119 / give-back 1120 / resume 1121 / holds 1124+1127 / lull give-back 1125 / resume 1126 / melt-up 1128 / SUNDAY give-back 1130 / resume 1201 / crest give-back 1202) - scheduled catalysts do NOT re-anchor the chain; the chain state off day-N-1 tape owns every day's NET. RESOLUTIONS (each n>=2 spanning groups): (P1) PHASE SHIFT = CATALYST CONTINUITY - new play timing.catalyst_continuity_frontrun: under a LIVE continuous weather catalyst (hard_heat ramp visible in the models) an armed turn/resume fires the NEXT session, front-running the discrete print/peak (1110exh->1111 G7, 1118armed->1119 G8); with no live ramp the resume WAITS for the discrete catalyst (0923->0924 hold->0925 Thu G3/4; 1029 stall->1030 Thu G6). The 1119/1120 and 1201/1202 'inversions' were chain-phase slips in one-shot mode, not rule failures: run off actual tape the chain pins 1120 as post-violent give-back and 1202 as the give-back off the 1201 extreme. (P2) RULE PRECEDENCE (1120): R2 was never a day-NET rule - R2 owns the post-print LEG side + the magnitude up-size; the day NET is owned by the chain (R1/R4). A print day after a violent prior-day extension pops WITH the swing and ROUND-TRIPS into an alternation give-back close (1001->1002 +900spike/-440close G4; 1119->1120 pop/-730 G8). All 12 storage Thursdays G3-G8 are consistent under this frame (11 leg-sided with the swing; 1120 leg-sided too). (P3) WINTER MAGNITUDE BANDS (live-cold-ramp regime, per-event): resume +1300..+2000 (1111 +1580, 1119 +1930, 1126 +1360); thin-holiday+hard_heat+delivery MELT-UP stack +1600..+2400 (1111, 1128 +2340 - thin AMPLIFIES a delivery day, early close does NOT cap); give-back splits by weather state: ramp-live/crest SHALLOW -700..-900 (1110, 1120, 1202) vs LULL (HDD flat/falling that day) DEEP -1500..-1800 (1117, 1125 -1770); non-catalyst resume stays +800..+1000 (0925, 0929, 1121, 1201); holds stay +-150 even in winter (0924, 1112, 1124, 1127). (P4) 1128 folded: thin+hard_heat+print = melt-up stack n=2 (1111, 1128); thin is an AMPLIFIER on delivery days, a damper on hold days (1013, 1127). (P5) 1124 solved: the weekend gap carries only NEW closure info - a shock already in the models (priced 1119-1121) adds ~nothing over the weekend (1123-24 ~+250, and the +390 Sunday jump was the Dec->Jan ROLL) vs 1109 +1560 when the shock was new that weekend; also the chain runs THROUGH Sunday sessions (1130 -590 took the post-1128 give-back, so 1201 opened resume-due). R1 REFINEMENTS: ramp arm - under a live ramp with intact swing legs a one-day give-back resumes regardless of close-recovery fraction (1120->1121 25%, 1125->1126 14%; 1110->1111 consistent); depth arm - at >=~70% swing retrace R5 capitulation OUTRANKS the R1 closes-at-low continuation read (0922->0923, 1016->1017, 1117->1118, 1125->1126). REFINED-vs-ACTUAL (per-event): 1119 +1600/+1930, 1120 -700/-730, 1121 +900/+910, 1124 +100/+80, 1125 -1600/-1770, 1126 +1400/+1360, 1127 +100/+160, 1128 +2000/+2340, 1201 +900/+890, 1202 -800/-710. Direction 10/10. IRREDUCIBLE: (a) extreme-day full magnitude (1119 +1930 vs band-high +1600; 1128 +2340 vs +2000) - the standing dominant residual; (b) hold-day sign inside +-150 (1124, 1127); (c) Sunday-session depth (1130 -590; thin-session R1 reads unreliable); (d) the one-shot chain PHASE itself - one violent surprise (1119) shifts the whole chain a day; only day-N-1 tape re-anchors it (the live-coach argument). meta.s98_2_refine_note: S98.2 UNBLINDED per-group refine of G9 (Dec3-31, the surplus-collapse block, the walk's FIRST BLOCK-LEAN MISS) - refined curves in forecasts/grp9.json (refined_* fields), derived ONLY from general rules + decision-state + prior-day ACTUAL tape; sizes from condition-class bands. THE HEADLINE: the block-lean killer is SOLVED as a GENERAL play - structure.chain_polarity_flip: (ARM, read at a swing-day close) PARABOLIC EXTENSION (run >=~1.5-2x the season's prior largest swing, >=~9 sessions, no origin-shelf touch: G9 +9700/12 sessions vs prior winter swings <=+5080; G4 +3690 = 1.6x G3; G5 -3770 = 1.7x) + BLOW-OFF (the extension day closes >=~30% off its intraday extreme: 1205 closed 31% off +3560; 1007 last-hour roll-over; mirror 1222 closed 72% off its low); (CONFIRM) the FIRST BAND-BREAKING counter day (net >=~1.5x its condition-class give-back band: 1208 -2730 vs -700..-900 = 3x; 1008 -1800; 1020 +2660; 1223 +5010) WITH old-direction continuation-collapse (1208 up-legs 3/33; 1008 up 0/15; 1020 down 1/10) - a weekend repricing AGAINST the armed crest counts as the counter delivery (1207 Sun gap -2380). After CONFIRM every polarity-relative rule (R1 resume, ramp arm, alternation, print side) reads in the NEW direction, and R5's origin shelf is VOID (1211 broke the 4.367 origin - post-parabolic it is a REVERSAL, not a give-back; contrast G7's non-parabolic give-back, 0.55x prior swing, which held its shelf and resumed). Back-checks: tops 1007/1008 (autumn) + 1205/1208 (winter); bottoms 1016->1019/1020 (autumn) + 1222/1223 (winter, terminated-to-BASING - the year-end caveat: no new lows after 1223 but no clean up-chain either). OTHER RESOLUTIONS: (1) FUNDAMENTAL INVERSION dissolves into ONE rule - prints NEVER own the side, the chain at its CURRENT POLARITY does (up-chain bought bearish prints 1106/1113/1128; down-chain sold bullish prints 1023/1211/1218/1224); at a priced parabolic extreme 1-3 sessions post-flip the confirming print is the EXIT-LIQUIDITY event (-1800..-4000: 1211 -3970). (2) THE 1204 CONTRA: a post-violent print day gives back only when the ramp crested at/before the print (1120, 1202, 1002); with the HDD stream still RISING through the print (26.9->30.3->30.5) the give-back lands INTRADAY and the catalyst wins the close (1204 +1100, morning -390). (3) THE SYMMETRIC BOUNDARY READ: R1 generalizes to EVERY session - close AT the extreme (<~10% recovery) -> chain continues (1208->1209, 1211->1212, 1212->1215, 1215->1216; miss 1209->1210 +370); close >=~35% off the extreme with a late counter-tick -> one-day alternation bounce (1216->1217 +1880, 1218->1219 +850, 1222->1223 +5010). (4) BOUNCES ARE NEVER EXTENDED in a mature chain - and a scheduled print following a violent counter-bounce delivers OLD-chain-side through it (1023, 1218, 1224 = the attack-6 verdict: chain polarity beats the young turn, n=3). (5) FAILED-RALLY TELL: a counter-chain spike that round-trips (1210 65%, 1230 91%) -> next session runs hard chain-side (1211 -3970, 1231 -2630; mirror 1002->1003). (6) CREST/CRASH BANDS set (see magnitude.crash_regime_bands); year-end thin = AMPLIFIER both ways, squaring is not a damper (1223/+5010, 1224/-2450, 1231/-2630). REFINED-vs-ACTUAL (per-event): 1203 +1400/+1520, 1204 +1000/+1100, 1205 +1800/+2440, 1208 -2400/-2730 (gap -1200/-2380+390), 1209 -2500/-2840, 1210 -700/+370 MISS, 1211 -2600/-3970, 1212 -1200/-1180, 1215 -1300/-1560, 1216 -1000/-1020, 1217 +1200/+1880, 1218 -1500/-1830, 1219 +600/+850, 1222 -500/-630, 1223 +2000/+5010, 1224 -1800/-2450, 1226 +500/+670, 1229 0/-10, 1230 +100/+180, 1231 -2000/-2630. Direction 19/20. IRREDUCIBLE: (a) 1210 +370 (third-day pause after two at-extreme-close crashes - the rules say continue; 1008->1009 continued in the identical state); (b) the extreme tails beyond band-high, now TWO-SIDED (1223 +5010 vs +2400 band-top; 1205 +2440/+3560; 1211 -3970) - the standing dominant residual; (c) the Sunday-gap SIZE (1207 -2380: direction callable off the armed crest, magnitude not); (d) the post-termination year-end regime (basing vs new up-chain: the 1222/1223 flip signature ended the down-chain - no new lows - but 1224/1231 still crashed; two-sided basing is not sequencable beyond one day). meta.s100_2_flip_characterization: THE CENTRAL DELIVERABLE - structure.chain_polarity_flip per instance, across every termination and near-termination in the walk. THE RULE IS KEPT AND IS USED ON THE INSTANCES ITS CONDITIONS DISCRIMINATE ON. C1 (band-break) WORKS EVERYWHERE TESTED: fires 1008 (-1800, 2x), 1020 (+2660), 1208 (-2730, 3x), 1223 (+5010, 2.6x), 0120 (+1930, 3.9x the day-2 bounce band); correctly declines 0107 (+1510, inside the +800..+1900 bounce band). Five fires, one correct decline, zero false positives spanning G4, G5, G9, G10 and G11 - C1 is the load-bearing condition and is sufficient on its own on every instance in the walk. C2 (old-side continuation-collapse) WORKS ON LOW-ACTIVITY TAPES and DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE ON HIGH-ACTIVITY TAPES: it fires correctly on 1008 (up 0/15), 1020 (dn 1/10, big 0/2), 1208 (up 3/33, big 2/6) and 1223 (dn 3/38, big 2/6), and it produces the sharpest correct rejection in the walk on 0107 (dn 10/36 with big down-legs 6/7 STILL ALIVE - the old side more alive than the new); but on 0120 it returns a FALSE NEGATIVE, with down legs still continuing ~64%. THE DISCRIMINATING CONDITION IS TAPE ACTIVITY, and the mechanism is that C2 is an absolute share-of-legs threshold applied to a leg count that varies tenfold across regimes: every instance C2 was calibrated on carries 15-98 legs on 15-25k trades per session, while G11's sessions carry 160-550 legs on 75-125k trades. On a high-activity tape both sides always retain a live share and a <=15% absolute threshold is mechanically unreachable. THE FIX IS A REFORMULATION, NOT A REMOVAL: express C2 as the RATIO of old-side to new-side continuation, which is scale-invariant and separates cleanly on fingerprint-comparable data (1020 0.00, 1208 0.40, 1223 0.42 vs the false 0107 at 1.23). G11 cannot yet be placed on that scale - month_characterize has not been run on the G11 tape - and that is a DECLARED BUILD GAP, not a result. C3 (never front-run) is forward-confirmed as a discipline: it correctly blocked the 0108 front-run and correctly withheld a flip at G11's 0119 and 0120 opens, and it does NOT block the flip at the 0121 open because the confirm had printed. C4 (catalyst arbiter) is forward-confirmed twice: 0109's chain-side delivery refuted the false flip, and G11's 0130 print - the surplus NARROWING 263->248, the first weekly print all winter to stop re-confirming the down-chain - supplied exactly the forward fundamental driver whose ABSENCE on 0107 correctly denied a birth. THE TERMINATION-vs-BIRTH SPLIT SURVIVES G11 INTACT and is strengthened: 0107 had no driver and yielded nothing; 0120 had an accelerating cold ramp adding at new horizons and later a confirming storage turn, and it yielded a chain. NOTE ON INFORMATION REQUIREMENTS: C1, C2 and C4 are ALL measurable at the confirm day's CLOSE, so the flip is open-time callable at the FOLLOWING session's open. The G11 miss is therefore as much a PROTOCOL residual as a rule residual - the one-shot blind protocol withholds the 0120 close that carries the confirm. Fourth independent appearance of the live-coach argument.

meta.s100_2_mos_characterization: FIRST-USE CHARACTERIZATION of the MOS weather_forecast block (three sign flips: 0123 helped, 0125 and 0126 hurt). PER-EVENT, AND EXPLICITLY NOT A VERDICT - weather_forecast stays in decision_state in full and permanently; the agent decides how to use it. No gating, down-weighting or quarantine is proposed or implied. WHAT THE RUN-DELTA DISCRIMINATES ON: FIRST-APPEARANCE adds - a shot entering at horizons that previously carried nothing. 0123 is the clean instance: +2.885 at Jan 27 and +4.500 at Jan 28, horizons empty the run before; the blind run took the up side against what its own chain read would have called, and HIT (+800 guessed, +1170 actual). 0119 is the same form one step earlier: +8.511 at Jan 24, the block's information event. WHAT IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE ON: REVISIONS to a shot already in the models and already priced. 0125 is the sharpest case - the -2.315 cut at Jan 30 drove an explicit negative-gap call and the actual gap was +2480, the block's largest; the shot being wobbled had been priced since 0119. 0126 is its mirror - the +3.197 re-add at the SAME horizon one run later flipped a carry-DOWN call that would have been right (actual -620). The two revisions cancel to approximately nothing within two runs, which is both the evidence and the mechanism: a market prices a shot once, and subsequent few-gw-HDD wobble at a horizon it already occupies is inside the noise the option/vol market has already absorbed. New play signal.mos_first_appearance_vs_revision, n=2 first-appearance and n=2 revision, all within G11 - ZERO forward evidence, must survive G12+ before it is treated as blind-applicable. A SEPARATE AND INDEPENDENT LIMITATION, not a property of the signal: the stream is D-1-EVENING and is therefore one model cycle BEHIND the weekend repricing (see s100_2_weekend_gap_note).
meta.s100_2_evidence_fields_note: S100.2 adds THREE FIELDS TO EVERY PLAY - `requires`, `scope`, `forward_evidence`. RATIONALE, load-bearing: most blind-versus-refined disagreements are not disagreements about the market at all, they are differences in what was KNOWABLE at decision time, and treating them as a precedence problem hides that. `requires` (open_time_only / needs_day_N-1_tape / needs_intraday_reveal) names the information a play consumes and dissolves those apparent conflicts. `scope` (leg side / day net / block lean / magnitude / gap / timing) names what a play OWNS, which is the correct precedence axis and the one S97.2 already settled when it gave R2 the post-print leg side and magnitude while the chain kept the day net. `forward_evidence` records whether a play has been confirmed on a block it was NOT derived from, and it is the field that GATES PROMOTION: refined rules are hindsight-fitted and carry zero forward evidence, so they must NEVER silently overwrite blind-applicable ones. Doing so would promote in-sample fits into the operating playbook untested, and it would destroy the blind-versus-refined GAP, which is itself the measurement of how much of the edge is sequential rather than open-time (G7 was 3/10 blind against 9/10 refined; R2 was 4/10 blind against 10/10 refined; G11 is 6/12 blind against 10/12 refined). A refined rule earns open-time status only by surviving a forward block. WHERE TWO PLAYS OVERLAP IN SCOPE WITHOUT A SETTLED BOUNDARY, THE OVERLAP IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN RESOLVED - see s100_2_scope_overlaps_flagged.
meta.s100_2_scope_overlaps_flagged: FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED - scope overlaps with no settled boundary, listed so they are not silently arbitrated. (1) structure.mature_swing_alternation and direction.giveback_exhaustion_boundary both claim the DAY NET of the session after an extreme, both require day-N-1 tape, and on G11's 0122 they agree only by accident (R4 called the give-back, R1's close read on 0121 said continue). No boundary is proposed. (2) structure.failed_rally_tell and direction.giveback_exhaustion_boundary both read a round-tripped session's close and reach OPPOSITE conclusions - the tell says the round-trip exhausts the counter side and the next session runs chain-side, R1 says a deep recovery means the give-back exhausted and the swing resumes. The unmodelled separator appears to be which POLARITY the round-tripping day belongs to, but the tell has never been tested at up-polarity, so this is a research finding, not a rule. (3) daytype.weekday_archetype and structure.post_parabolic_bleed both offer a day-net class band; the brain already says the archetype is overridden by the chain, which is a precedence statement rather than a scope split, and it is left as is.
meta.s100_2_same_information_conflicts: GENUINE CONFLICTS - plays that are BOTH open_time_only and make OPPOSITE calls on the SAME information. These are NOT resolved by precedence; one is wrong or an unmodelled condition separates them, and they are recorded as research findings. (1) THE G11 BLOCK-OPEN CONFLICT: structure.post_parabolic_bleed (open_time_only) said the carried down-polarity holds until a confirm prints, and timing.catalyst_continuity_frontrun (open_time_only) said a live accelerating ramp fires the next session. On 0119-0121 they pointed opposite ways on identical open-time information. The blind run took the bleed and lost the block. The candidate separator is whether the ramp is adding at FIRST-APPEARANCE horizons or merely being revised - which is the new mos play - but that is derived on this same block and therefore cannot also adjudicate it. UNRESOLVED. (2) THE 0125 GAP-SIGN CONFLICT: daytype.monday_weekend_gap's priced-shock arm and the raw realized-cold read in decision_state.weather pointed opposite ways on the same Sunday, and the blind run explicitly recorded that it was rejecting the realized-cold read, which was the side that paid. Neither play owns the gap sign cleanly. UNRESOLVED, and it is the specific reason magnitude.weekend_gap_delivery is written to give the gap SIGN to the running chain rather than to either weather read.
meta.s100_2_irreducibles: DECLARED IRREDUCIBLE for G11, each with its mechanism. (a) THE WEEKEND-GAP MAGNITUDE on a fresh-shot weekend (0118 +2100, 0125 +2480): the repricing is priced off the Sat/Sun 00Z/12Z model cycle and decision_state carries only the D-1-evening run - the market is one model cycle ahead of the state variable. A DATA BUILD closes it, no reasoning does. (b) THE CRESTING-RAMP PAUSE PAIR (0127 -260, 0128 -400): under a cresting ramp R1's two arms disagree - the depth arm reads exhaustion and resume, the last-hour arm reads continuation - and the day nets sit inside +-500 where the boundary read carries no edge. Two consecutive sign misses inside that band is the honest result; no rule is added to capture them, because any rule that did would be fitted to two days. (c) THE EXTREME-DAY MAGNITUDE (0121 +3820 against a band top of 3000; 0130 +5020 against 2200) - the standing dominant residual of the entire walk, now two-sided and confirmed on every block since G6. (d) 0130 SPECIFICALLY carries an unmodelled driver: the expiring February contract ran 3.0 -> 5.4 into delivery and a delivery squeeze was pulling the strip, while the forecaster carries NO state variable exposing front-month expiry, open-interest concentration or the Feb/Mar calendar spread. That is a MISSING STATE VARIABLE with a named fix, not an unforecastable event - and it is the highest-value addition to decision_state this pass identified. (e) THE FLIP-CONFIRM PHASE in one-shot mode: C1 was measurable only at the 0120 close, which the one-shot protocol withholds - the standing protocol residual, fourth appearance.

reasoning_method.note: HOW he reasons - the general method applied every day. Per-event, never averaged; drift is a DESCRIPTOR tied to conditions, never point-fit.
reasoning_method.continuous_frame: Reason CONTINUOUSLY, one day into the next. Each day's forecast FLOWS from the prior day's close + trajectory + running state - a continuation-or-turn of the running path, never a from-flat isolated event. CAUTION (s95_2): the continuous data series contains CONTRACT ROLLS (~monthly) that inject a fake overnight jump (G3-5: the Sep24->25 +0.276 Oct->Nov roll). At a known roll boundary forecast the REAL overnight ~0 and reason on roll-clean intraday nets; never read a roll jump as a market move / swing turn.
reasoning_method.anchor: Start each block from the ACTUAL hr24 of the day BEFORE the block (blind-safe). Within the block, each day flows from the agent's OWN prior-day guessed close.
reasoning_method.block_open_lean: At a block boundary, LEAN AGAINST a stretched swing - but the trigger is SWING EXHAUSTION, not the calendar seam: weight a reversal when the running (roll-clean) path is at a cum-EXTREME AND the old block's LAST 1-2 days show a counter-move (0923 bounce + 0924 hold before the G3->G4 up-turn; 1007 last-hour roll-over before the G4->G5 crash). The reversal is delivered through the INTRADAY US SESSIONS (G3->G4 first week) or as an intraday US-session CRASH (1008), and occasionally pre-loaded by a real overnight/weekend GAP (1019 +1570). Do NOT extend the trend into a stretched seam; do NOT blind-fade a still-trending block with no last-day counter-move. G6 CAVEAT: this reversion is a GIVE-BACK, not a sustained reversal - the block can itself V back (G5, G6), so do not marry the new lean past its own exhaustion. Confirm with intraday flow.
reasoning_method.fundamentals_role: Storage surplus/deficit + HDD/CDD regime = a SLOW, WEAK block-trajectory backdrop, NEVER a day-level or pre-print side/timing signal. The +150 Bcf surplus called G3 down. BUT (G6, load-bearing): near the seasonal (autumn->winter) transition the surplus is an UNRELIABLE block-direction cue - rising HDD (heating demand) flipped the block UP through G4/Oct and won in G6 despite the bearish surplus. Treat fundamentals as a lean of last resort, dominated by the running trajectory and the swing-exhaustion read.
reasoning_method.daytype_priors: Monday = BIG mover, but the weekend repricing arrives at the SUNDAY reopen gap and Monday's US session is the REACTION (R3: fade a mature-swing gap, extend a fresh-turn gap, else carry Friday's side) - the old 'often a REVERSAL' lean is retired (G7: both Mondays continued). Thin-holiday size-down only with NO active weather catalyst (1013 yes, 1111 no). Storage Thursday = large dominant leg at/after the 10:30 ET print, size UP; SIDE = the running swing/turn state, never the print sign (R2, 10/10 G3-G7). Fri = range (overridden in a high-momentum reversal regime AND by R4 give-back-after-extreme: 1107, 1114). Tue = strongest-trend weekday. Wed = weak up-lean (overridden by block trend). Never pool across DOW.
reasoning_method.intraday_side: OPEN-time from-flat side is a coin-flip (stays OPEN). WITHIN the day the side is CALLED by (1) dip_imb_level flow nowcast (held legs' flow sign matches leg dir near-perfect) and (2) CONTINUATION-ASYMMETRY (true-direction legs continue, counter-dir die). A counter-trend GRIND is real (block trend does not veto it) - BUT it is NOT callable AT THE OPEN (0916, G6 week-2): no open-time signal distinguishes a counter-trend grind from a continuation day. CAVEAT: flow_nowcast LAGS an extreme gap melt-up (1020 7/12) - lean on continuation-asymmetry there. Shape (grind holds / peaked_fast spike fades, 23/24) decides hold-vs-close.
reasoning_method.magnitude_sizing: Size per event vs the running trajectory + regime; do NOT globally rescale. The under-forecast is CONCENTRATED on three catalyst conditions - weekend-gap Monday, storage Thursday, swing-reversal/seam - which run to MULTIPLES of default; non-catalyst chop is sized ~right. Stack the up-sizers when they coincide (1020: Monday + reversal + swing-turn). G6 CONFIRMS magnitude is the DOMINANT residual error (undersized both the dip and the recovery) - even after condition-sorting, expect to under-size the extremes; do NOT clip the ride. Use the $350 staircase as the real-time continuation read.
reasoning_method.shape_and_exit: A slow GRIND holds; a front-loaded peaked_fast SPIKE round-trips (fingerprint-confirmed 23/24). REVISED: turn_far_thinning did NOT confirm as the live recruitment/exit discriminator - treat it as a diagnostic only. Use continuation/retention + peaked_fast + flow for the running turn.
reasoning_method.discipline: PER-EVENT only, never average/pool/count. Drift is a DESCRIPTOR - tie each miss to its CONDITIONS, never point-fit. GENERAL rules (mechanism + n) only.
reasoning_method.swing_exhaustion_reversion: GENERAL mechanism, fingerprint-CONFIRMED via a CONTINUATION-COLLAPSE signature: at a swing turn the OLD-direction legs STOP continuing and turn_exhaustion goes negative, while the NEW direction begins to hold at the extreme. Named: G4->G5 top 1008 (old-swing UP 0/15 - total exhaustion, dominant DOWN 12/26); G5 V-bottom 1016 (UP recruits hold 5/18 on a down-close day); intra-block 0916 (block-DOWN legs 1/11) and G3 0922 low -> 0923 bounce. The turn begins in the old swing's last legs and completes through the INTRADAY sessions (G3->G4) or as an intraday US-session CRASH (1008), sometimes pre-loaded by a real overnight/weekend GAP (1019 +1570). CORRECTION (s95_2): the previously-cited '0925 +2760 overnight gap' delivery form is VOID - that was the Oct->Nov contract roll, NOT a swing turn. Do NOT extend trend into a stretched swing; watch for the old-direction continuation-collapse. G6: the reversion is a GIVE-BACK - a block can V back, so treat each leg of the swing as its own exhaustible move.
reasoning_method.magnitude_catalyst_sort: GENERAL: sort the big days by CONDITION, do not rescale. UP-size on weekend-gap Monday, storage Thursday, and swing-reversal/seam days. DOWN-size on thin-holiday Monday (1013), Sunday carry, non-catalyst chop. Compound the up-sizers when they coincide (1020). G6: still expect to under-size the extremes - magnitude is the dominant residual.
reasoning_method.giveback_exhaustion_boundary: R1 (S96.2, the sequencing solvent): read the give-back's OWN close. EXHAUSTED = closes >=~40-50% off its intraday extreme + last-hours counter-tick + no continuation-collapse in the underlying swing's big legs -> next session RESUMES the swing (size up if a catalyst day). NOT exhausted = closes at/near its extreme with last hours extending -> give-back CONTINUES. If the swing side's own legs have already collapsed (0915 down 0/8), stand down - the swing is suspect, no resume call. n: resume 1105->1106, 1107->1109gap, 1110->1111, 1112->1113 (G7), 0926->0929, 1003->1005 (G4); continue 1002->1003 (G4), 1114->1117 (G7); filter 0915->0916 (G3). Mechanism: a give-back is positioning unwind inside an intact flow regime - when the unwind cannot hold its lows into the close, the sellers are done and the dominant flow re-asserts; the last hour is the earliest tell (hr24->hr1).
reasoning_method.mature_swing_alternation: R4 (S96.2): swing AGE gates day-sequencing. YOUNG swing (<=3 sessions since the turn) chains extensions day-after-day (0929/0930/1001 G4; 1030/1031/1103/1104 G6). MATURE swing (>=4 sessions): a material fresh extreme close (>= ~$300 beyond the prior extreme) is NEVER followed by a consecutive extension - the next session is a give-back/hold (G7 5/5: 1104->1105, 1106->1107, 1109->1110, 1111->1112, 1113->1114; 1007->1008 G4). Then R1 decides whether the give-back exhausts (resume) or runs (continue). Mechanism: early in a swing the repricing is under-done (info still propagating); late, each new extreme exhausts the marginal buyer - swing-exhaustion in incremental form.
reasoning_method.weekend_gap_reaction: R3 (S96.2): the weekend repricing is delivered AT THE SUNDAY REOPEN as the gap - Monday's US session is the REACTION, not the repricing. Gap WITH a mature swing to a fresh cum-extreme -> Monday FADES it (1109 +1560 -> 1110 -820; 0908 +460 -> faded +740->+190). Gap at a FRESH turn (<=~2 sessions old) -> Monday EXTENDS (1019 +1570 -> 1020 +2660). No material gap -> Monday carries FRIDAY's side (1107->1110, 1114->1117 G7; 0919->0922 G3; 1017->1020 G5). Monday bigness stands; Monday-as-block-reversal is retired (the G3-5 'reversals' were swing-state coincidences).
reasoning_method.giveback_origin_shelf_floor: R5 (S96.2): a terminal give-back runs until it retraces to the swing's ORIGIN/consolidation shelf, then stabilizes (give-back-not-reversal). At >=~75% retrace of the swing, the R1 closes-at-low continuation read INVERTS: capitulation closes at stretched extremes precede the BOUNCE (0922->0923 +610 G3; 1016->1017 +740 G5; 1117->1118 +270 G7; also 1029 stall -> 1030 +2580 G6 as the Thursday-turn form). Mechanism: the give-back unwinds the crowd that entered during the extension; once price returns to where the extension began there is no trapped inventory left to force further. Use for give-back sizing (floor) and for calling the stabilization/turn day. S98.2 CAVEAT: the shelf floor holds only for NON-parabolic give-backs (G7). After a confirmed polarity flip off a parabolic run the shelf is VOID and breaks (1211 through 4.367) - the break itself is the flip's confirmation.
reasoning_method.chain_polarity: S98.2 + S99.2 HARDENED (the G9+G10 lessons, load-bearing): every sequencing rule is POLARITY-RELATIVE - 'resume' means resume the RUNNING chain's direction, and BANDS are polarity-relative too (ramp-shallow give-backs belong to up-chains; a live cold ramp in a down-chain is the COUNTER catalyst - it feeds 1-2 day bounces and full crash-band days when they die: 0114). The polarity flips ONLY at a confirmed structure.chain_polarity_flip passing the HARDENED four-condition bar (band-break >=1.5x + old-side continuation-collapse in the actual tape + printed-not-front-run + the catalyst-arbiter/backdrop check) - a strong in-band bounce is NEVER a flip (0107, 1217, 1223-as-birth). TERMINATION does not equal BIRTH: without a forward fundamental driver a terminated chain enters the POST-PARABOLIC BLEED at the old polarity (see structure.post_parabolic_bleed) - the down-chain 'ends' only on the tape, never in the lean, until a true confirm prints. In a flipped/down regime: cold-delivery days FAIL, bullish prints SELL (8/8), and R1's symmetric close-vs-extreme read runs the alternation - reading CHAIN-SIDE days' closes only (a counter/fade day's recovered close carries no bounce signal: 0105).
reasoning_method.post_parabolic_bleed: S99.2 (the G10 class): after a parabolic chain's termination signature fires WITHOUT a birth driver, the regime is neither trend-chain nor two-sided basing but a stepped BLEED at the old polarity: single crash days, 1-2 day bounces (never 3), post-crash pauses, more small days, marginal new lows. Sequencing: bounce-death + failed_rally_tell -> crash; crash -> pause (crashes chain only INTO a print day); print days chain-sided and, on in-chain confirmations, sized DOWN a class. The bleed persists as long as the fundamental stream keeps re-confirming the old chain (G10: the whole block).

The rungs ($50 / $150 / $250 / $350 / $500 of peak_usd) are genuine numeric thresholds, but peak_usd is a leg's realized-so-far favourable excursion inside a live 1800s window; it exists in renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json and in no decision_state. audit.argument: A conditional continuation rate that rises with the favourable peak already reached: $50->0.43, $150->0.57, $250->0.75, $350->0.92, $500->1.00, derived on 372 legs over 12 warm-season days (S92), n=38 at the $350 rung and n=11 at $500. 'continuation' is defined in month_characterize.move_path as retention >= 0.5 where retention = end-of-1800s-window favourable excursion divided by peak. That is a real rate on a real conditioning variable and it is the one play in this batch that can be re-run, because renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json stores peak_usd, retention, continuation, time_to_peak_s and peaked_fast for 6,358 legs across 108 days - 98 of which post-date the derivation window. I re-ran it. THE SHAPE SURVIVES PERFECTLY AND THE LEVELS DO NOT: 0.386 / 0.519 / 0.626 / 0.713 / 0.823 against the claimed 0.43 / 0.57 / 0.75 / 0.92 / 1.00, monotone at every rung, with the shortfall widening as size rises (-0.04 at $50, -0.21 at $350, -0.18 at $500). The headline the runbook carries - 'the $350 crossing = a 92% keep-riding event; $500 = 100%' - is a small-n artifact; at n=1,307 and n=638 the true rates are 71% and 82%. Per cell, never pooled, the $350 rung holds at 0.701 hard_heat / 0.758 mod_heat / 0.652 unknown / 0.723 up-legs / 0.702 down-legs, so it is a stable relationship, not a regime accident. THE CAUSAL READING IS THE PART THAT DOES NOT HOLD: within a fixed 1800s window, median time-to-peak climbs monotonically with the peak bucket (12s / 454s / 924s / 1,146s / 1,343s / 1,521s), and since retention is end-over-peak, a leg that peaks at 1,521 of 1,800 seconds has only 279 seconds left in which to give back. Holding size fixed, timing dominates: in the 150-350 bucket peaked_fast legs continue 2 of 32 (0.063) against 729 of 1,863 (0.391) for slow peaks, a six-fold spread; in the 50-150 bucket, 6 of 226 (0.027) against 231 of 1,491 (0.155). So the staircase is largely SIZE ACTING AS A PROXY FOR TIME-TO-PEAK, which is what shape.grind_vs_spike already says causally ('grind holds, front-loaded spike round-trips'). The play also declares its own tension and I want that on the record as honesty rather than as a defect: status STABLE, confidence 0.90, forward_evidence 'NONE beyond derivation... Its high confidence reflects derivation strength, not forward evidence.'
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, emphatically, and I made it try. A mean-reverting tape would have produced a flat or descending staircase; it did not, at 6,358 legs, on 98 days outside the derivation window, and per cell. The rung LEVELS did come out otherwise - every one of them, in the same direction - which is exactly what a falsifiable measurement is supposed to be able to do. What could NOT have come out otherwise is the causal attribution to size: nothing in the derivation separates size from time-to-peak, and when I separate them the timing variable carries most of the effect.

audit.argument: Two-part record. The ORIGINAL arm (turn_far_thinning = far-ladder change reads the running turn) was tested on the S95 fingerprint pass and DEMOTED to noise - a real falsification, executed, recorded, and the play rewritten around it. I reproduced that demotion off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json: across all 6,358 committed legs, legs that CONTINUED carry a 37.4% negative-turn_far_thinning share and legs that FADED carry 30.7%. A 6.7-point separation on n=6,358 is not a discriminator, and the sign of the difference runs AGAINST the arm's original direction (the turning legs are the LESS far-thinned ones). The demotion was correct and if anything understated. The SURVIVING arm (old-swing continuation-collapse + negative turn_exhaustion + peaked_fast) rests on one named instance, 1008 old-swing up-legs 0/15, which reproduces EXACTLY: 20251008 carries 15 up legs and 0 continued, against 12 of 26 down legs continuing on the same day. That is an argued mechanism (the old swing stops recruiting before price turns) with a traced first instance, which is NOVEL_N1 by the rubric's own discriminator - not ASSERTED. What it is NOT is MECHANISM_VERIFIED: there is no base rate, no non-turn control day, and no measured hit-rate for the surviving arm on its own. The record itself scopes it further - the surviving measurement is the SAME quantity as chain_polarity_flip C2 and inherits C2's G11 false negative and the S100.3 finding that it is non-discriminating on the 0107/0120 tape class.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, decisively, for the demoted arm - it was tested and it failed, and the play was rewritten to say so. That is the strongest single signal in this batch that the desk's measurements are real. NO for the surviving arm as currently supported: 0/15 is a striking number but it is one hand-picked turn day with no control, so nothing in the present evidence could have refuted the continuation-collapse read. The base rate that would settle it is computable from the same committed file and has never been computed.

legacy_notes.conditions_note: REAL BAR, UNSERVED QUANTITY. peaked_fast is defined as time-to-peak <= 60s, a genuine numeric threshold that splits 1,246 of 6,358 legs in the fingerprint store. But time_to_peak_s, peaked_fast and retention are per-leg fields in fingerprints.json; decision_state carries no time-to-peak at any grain, so the bar cannot be evaluated at the moment the forecast is made. This is the play's own caveat ('usable once the first ~60s-2h of build is seen - NOT at the open') restated as a data fact, and it is why every modern appearance of the play is a needs_intraday_reveal stand-down.

audit.argument: MECHANISM: a front-loaded capture means the move is already paid for and round-trips; a slow build is continuous repricing that holds. SUPPORT: a per-leg rate on the committed fingerprint store, and I reproduced it independently. Across all 108 days / 6,358 legs in renders/ng_refine_s95/fingerprints.json, legs with peaked_fast=true (time-to-peak <= 60s) fail to hold (retention < 0.5 at the 1800s horizon) on 1,234 of 1,246 = 99.0%; only 12 held. On the 6 pivotal days the brain names, 39 of 40 peaked_fast legs faded (the brain's '23/24' is a narrower subset of the same set). The relationship is MONOTONE across four time-to-peak buckets: hold rate 1.0% (0-60s) -> 5.8% (60-300s) -> 16.1% (300-900s) -> 59.2% (900-1800s). TWO QUALIFICATIONS THE RECORD DOES NOT MAKE. (a) The two limbs are not symmetric: the SPIKE-FADES limb is near-deterministic, but the GRIND-HOLDS limb is a minority outcome - non-peaked_fast legs hold only 1,915 of 5,112 = 37.5% pooled, and reach 59% only in the slowest bucket. 'A slow GRIND holds (ride)' overstates its own evidence. (b) Retention is measured at a fixed 1800s horizon, so a peak at 60s has 1,740s to decay while a peak at 1,700s has 100s; part of the gradient is definitional. The monotone ordering survives that, the 1%-vs-59% headline does not fully. THE CONTRADICTION: the play's scope says 'leg side + hold-vs-fade (intraday); NOT the day net', yet its G11 FORWARD-CONFIRMED line reads 'both sides HIT' on two DAY NETS - a quantity the play excludes by its own words, on a day it oversized 2.9x.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, emphatically, and this is the strongest single measurement in the batch. The hold rate could have been flat across the four time-to-peak buckets, or inverted, or the 12 spike-legs that held could have been 400. It is monotone across 6,358 legs on 108 days, and I computed it from the raw fingerprint store rather than reading the claim. The G11 arm is the exception: 'both sides hit' on 2 day nets could not have falsified a leg-level shape claim in either direction, and it is credited to the play anyway.

forward.text: NEGATIVE-TO-INERT forward. Across G6-G11 the surprise SIGN has been wrong on side wherever it was consulted, which is the play's own stated caveat, and its magnitude arm is subsumed by daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude. Kept as the record that surprise sign does not sort direction.

But each value is carried unchanged on roughly five consecutive sessions until the next Thursday print, so on any given day it is a weekly CONSTANT and cannot discriminate that day from its four neighbours - the quantity the play conditions on has zero within-week variance. Worse, on the print Thursday itself the served value is the PREVIOUS week's by construction (verified: on 20260528 the state serves 1.6 and on 20260529 it becomes -3.2), so the one day the play most wants to size is the one day the field is stale. g18 and g19 serve it null on all 20 days.

legacy_notes.forward_evidence: NEGATIVE-TO-INERT forward. Across G6-G11 the surprise SIGN has been wrong on side wherever it was consulted, which is the play's own stated caveat, and its magnitude arm is subsumed by daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude. Kept as the record that surprise sign does not sort direction.
legacy_notes.conditions_note: THE QUANTITY IS SERVED BUT THE PLAY STATES NO BAR. stor_surprise resolves in the modern states, but the call - 'big |surprise| -> bigger-leg day; near-consensus -> range/chop' - is qualitative, and the 10 Bcf split that appears in the falsifier is the S112 auditor's own construction for a refutation test (r = 0.087, big-surprise median BELOW small-surprise median), not the play's threshold. Two further reasons not to manufacture one. (a) PROSE-VS-SERVED DISAGREEMENT: the read says '|stor_surprise| (Bcf vs SEASONAL)' while the mechanism it describes requires a surprise vs CONSENSUS; the state serves both, and storage_consensus.last_print.surprise_vs_consensus_bcf is the quantity the market actually prices. (b) DEGENERATE WITHIN THE WEEK: verified directly on grp20-grp23_state.json, stor_surprise is carried unchanged across ~5 consecutive sessions and on the print Thursday itself is still the PREVIOUS week's value (g22 serves -5.0 on 0625 and only becomes -1.4 on 0626), so any bar written on it has zero within-week variance and is stale on the one day the play most wants to size.

audit.argument: Two arms. (a) MAGNITUDE: a big |stor_surprise| implies a bigger-leg day, near-consensus implies range/chop. (b) SIGN: the surprise sign does NOT sort direction. The entire evidence field is `distinct_prints: 6` - a count of the SAMPLE, not a measurement of the EFFECT - plus one exemplar, 0820, which is a counterexample supporting arm (b)'s negative claim rather than support for arm (a). No mechanism is argued for why surprise magnitude should scale the leg; the `call` field restates the rule. The forward field is candid: NEGATIVE-TO-INERT, and the magnitude arm is 'subsumed by daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude'. I MEASURED THE MAGNITUDE ARM. stor_surprise is served on 40 days across grp20-grp23_state.json (g18 and g19 carry it null on every day - the S107 empty-storage hole). corr(|stor_surprise|, |day_move_usd|) = 0.087 on n=40. Split at 10 Bcf: |surp|>=10 gives mean |dm| 648 / median 520 (n=10); |surp|<10 gives mean 554 / median 610 (n=30) - the mean lifts trivially and the MEDIAN runs backwards. On the 9 first-served days (the day a new surprise becomes open-time knowable) the two largest surprises, 33.0 and 39.2, delivered 620 and 410, while 9.4 delivered 1,340; r = 0.255 on n=9. SEPARATELY, AND MORE SERIOUSLY, THE INSTRUMENT IS THE WRONG QUANTITY: `read` says '|stor_surprise| (Bcf vs seasonal)' and the served field is indeed vs the 5-year norm, while the market prices vs CONSENSUS, which the same state block serves as storage_consensus.next_print.consensus_chg_bcf.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The record's own evidence, NO. 'distinct_prints: 6' cannot fail - it is the sample size. The one exemplar is a refutation of the sign arm, so it is evidence AGAINST a different arm, not evidence FOR this one. My measurement, YES, and it came out flat: an r of 0.087 on 40 days with the big-surprise median BELOW the small-surprise median is exactly what a null looks like. Arm (b), the negative claim that the sign does not sort, IS supported by the same data and could have failed: across g20-g23 the 20 days served an 'above' (bearish) surprise closed up 12 times and the 19 scorable days served a 'below' (bullish) surprise closed up 8 times - the fundamental sign is if anything inverted, so the negative claim survives.

audit.argument: Two separable arms. (i) SIZE: up-size the storage-Thursday magnitude prior. (ii) SIDE: the post-print LEG sides with the running chain, never the print sign, and the DAY NET is owned by the chain state. The SIZE arm is measurable and I measured it (below). The SIDE arm is the problem and it is the reason for the class. Its evidence field is a 10,000-character per-event narrative whose every entry has the form 'date, realized net, the chain was X, so the chain won' - the chain label is read at the same moment as the outcome, and the rule is confirmed by the outcome. Not one count in that block could have gone the other way. More telling: every counterexample produced a NEW conditioning dimension rather than a refutation. 1120 became the leg-vs-net split (S97.2); the G9 bullish-draw sells became polarity (S98.2); 0129/0205/0212 became spent-chain scoping (S101.3); the G14 blind became chain-state-is-tape-state (S102.1); 0326 became an entirely new play (magnitude.shoulder_counter_print_damping). Five successive rescues, each on n<=3. The forward field's headline '14 storage Thursdays, every one leg-sided with the running chain' is a 14/14 record for a rule the same file documents breaking at 1120, 0129 and 0326 - the 14/14 survives only because each break was first reclassified into a different arm.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: SIZE arm: YES, and I ran it - it could have come back at parity and it did not (1.65x pooled), and it DOES come back badly per-block in the two summer blocks. SIDE arm: NO. 'The chain won' is unfalsifiable once the chain can be relabelled live / spent / young / basing after the fact, and the play's own history is a record of exactly that relabelling. The leg-side arm is also not independently re-measurable from the committed corpus: g<N>_mbo_evidence.json serves three coarse phases per day (sflow / pxchg / vol), not a print-anchored decomposition, so nobody can recompute 'leg-sided with the chain' from the record even if they wanted to.

legacy_notes.conditions_note: NO BAR EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE PLAY. The trigger is 'when sizing the expected dominant-move magnitude', which is every day; the read is the blind's own per-day magnitude error; and the call is an explicit instruction NOT to act ('CANDIDATE correction ONLY... Do NOT globally rescale', deferring the actual sort to magnitude.catalyst_condition_sort). The play's own health field reaches the same conclusion in its own words: 'there is no numeric bar... it never selects a subset of days, and it never emits a number.' The only figures in the record are five realized guess-vs-actual pairs (1008 +320/-1980, 1010 +150/-1490, 1016 -300/-1190, 1020 +580/+2770, 1021 +440/+1100) - OUTCOMES logged after the fact, not a quantity readable at the open. A residual log is not a condition, and the audit further shows two of the five are wrong-SIGN days, so they do not even measure scale. Writing any bar here would be pure manufacture.

audit.argument: The entire support is a list of five days on which the blind's guess was smaller than the realized move, with the conclusion 'on catalyst days the actual dominant move DWARFED the guess'. I traced all five to forecasts/grp5.json and every number is exact: 1008 guess +320 / actual -1,980; 1010 +150 / -1,490; 1016 -300 / -1,190; 1020 +580 / +2,770; 1021 +440 / +1,100. So the evidence is real and honestly recorded. But it is a RESIDUAL LOG, not a test - the evidence field is the forecast error, and the claim is that the forecast error exists. AND THE LOG DOES NOT MEASURE WHAT THE PLAY CLAIMS: two of the five exemplars are WRONG-SIGN days, not undersized days. On 1008 the guess was +320 and the actual was -1,980; on 1010 the guess was +150 and the actual was -1,490. A day whose sign was wrong carries no information about whether the magnitude scale is too small, and folding two sign misses into a five-item scale claim inflates it by 40%. Only 1016 (4x under), 1020 (4.8x under) and 1021 (2.5x under) are right-signed under-calls and can bear the argument. To the play's credit it refuses to act on itself - status HYPOTHESIS, confidence 0.30, call 'CANDIDATE correction ONLY... Do NOT globally rescale', an explicit ANTI-LOCK-IN clause holding a rival reading (higher-vol autumn regime) open, and forward_evidence 'SUPERSEDED... Winter bands replaced it from G7 onward.' I considered NOT_A_PLAY on those grounds and rejected it: it has a trigger, a read and a call, it makes a substantive magnitude claim, and classifying it out would lose the finding about its evidence.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: No. Every item is a realized forecast error on a day chosen because the error was large. There is no denominator - the days on which the warm-season guess was the right size, or too big, were never counted - and no control regime. The one part that COULD have come out otherwise is the sign audit I ran on the play's own list, and it came out against the play: 2 of 5 exemplars are sign misses masquerading as scale misses.

plays.trigger: at a BLOCK boundary, when setting the block-level directional lean
plays.read: the running (roll-clean) path at a cum-EXTREME + a counter-move in the old swing's LAST 1-2 days + last-hour momentum into the seam - NOT the calendar seam alone
plays.call: LEAN AGAINST a stretched swing, do NOT extend it. Trigger on SWING EXHAUSTION (cum-extreme + last-1-2-day counter-move). The reversal is delivered through the INTRADAY sessions (G3->G4) or as an intraday US-session CRASH (1008), occasionally pre-loaded by a real overnight/weekend GAP (1019). It is a GIVE-BACK - the block can V back. Do NOT blind-fade a still-trending block with no last-day counter-move; confirm with intraday flow.
plays.requires: open_time_only
plays.scope: block lean
plays.caveats: Reframed to SWING-EXHAUSTION reversion (n=5, spanning autumn + the G6 winter-transition holdout). Roll-corrected: the G3->G4 turn came through the sessions, not an overnight gap. G6 confirms the week-1 give-back DIRECTION but the intra-block counter-turn (week-2 recovery) is UNSOLVED - same failure mode as 0916. Two delivery forms (intraday build/crash primary; overnight/weekend gap secondary). Do NOT harden into 'always fade the last block'. Confidence 0.4->0.42 (one true holdout half-confirmed). Winter/backwardation remains the decisive test. S96.2: the trigger's two arms are now operational - R4 (mature-swing extreme) arms the WATCH, the last-hours roll-over (1007, 1113) arms the FIRE; R5 (origin shelf / >=75% retrace) bounds the give-back and calls the stabilization day. Confidence 0.42->0.45 (G7 armed-trigger fired correctly on 1114/1117/1118). S98.2: the terminal-crest question this play circled is now owned by structure.chain_polarity_flip - this play remains the block-boundary GIVE-BACK lean; the flip play decides when a give-back is instead a reversal.

legacy_notes.conditions_note: OPERANDS UNSERVED AND NO THRESHOLD WRITTEN - both disqualifiers hold independently. The read is 'the running (roll-clean) path at a cum-EXTREME + a counter-move in the old swing's LAST 1-2 days + last-hour momentum into the seam'. All three are price-path content and none appears in the vocabulary: I searched it for cum_, last_hour, close_off, retrace and swing/chain age and there is no such path. The nearest-looking candidates are vol_regime.n0_prev_net and n0_net_sigma_5/10/20, and naming either would be the hole-#8 error twice over: (a) a prior-session net is a different quantity from a close measured against a running extreme, and (b) I checked the served values - vol_regime carries masked_one_shot true and is FROZEN at the block-anchor vintage, so n0_prev_date reads 2026-06-19 and n0_prev_net reads -80 on all ten days of G22 alike. It is constant by construction, i.e. degenerate before it is even mis-scoped. Separately the play states no number at all: 'a stretched swing' and 'cum-extreme' are qualitative, so even a served operand would have no bar to attach to. Its health field records the consequence: 0 fires in 60 days across G17-G23.

audit.argument: The claim is: at a block boundary, lean AGAINST a stretched swing when the running path is at a cum-extreme AND the old swing shows a counter-move in its last 1-2 days AND last-hour momentum rolls over. The support is 'n=5 turns across 4 blocks' plus a per-event chronology - and the chronology is a list of days SELECTED BECAUSE THEY TURNED, with the mechanism rewritten after each block to fit what happened: after G6 it became 'a GIVE-BACK, not a sustained reversal'; after G7 'the give-back can be one day deep'; the caveats field then records five successive reframes and ends by conceding the play has been SUPERSEDED as a block-lean caller and 'is retained as the historical record of the seam lean'. That is the reframe-to-fit signature, and no amount of arithmetic accuracy cures it. || AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ACCURATE - I checked all of it. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/g3g4g5_rt.json: 0925 +740, 0929 +950, 1001 +1170, 1008 -1800, 0923 +610, 0924 +50, 0922 cum -2250 (the G3 extreme) - every figure exact. The '1019 +1570 overnight gap' is exact as a GAP (net that session was -50), so the play is quoting the right field. Off research/kalshi/renders/ng_refine_s95/g7_rt.json the entire G7 forward arm is exact to the dollar: 1113 cum +2810 with an intraday peak +1160 closing +620 (the last-hour roll-over), 1114 -910, 1117 -1500, 1118 +270 stabilization, retrace -2590. Two figures I could NOT reproduce ('1007 +2120 roll-clean' vs the unadjusted +1360; '1016 -3770 roll-clean' vs -1100) are cited as roll-clean and the rt line declares itself NOT roll-adjusted, so that is a basis difference, not an error - I am not scoring it against the play. || WHAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING WORSE than OUTCOME_CREDITED is one genuine arming discipline: in research/kalshi/forecasts/grp7_seq_experiment.json the trigger sat HALF-lit at a cum-extreme (1104 up-legs healthy, no continuation-collapse) and the run DECLINED to fade - and the record shows the trigger then stayed half-armed through the block's later extremes until 1113. A trigger that visibly refuses to fire is doing real work. But it is one instance and the play no longer owns the decision.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the n=5 evidence base - those five turns are the definition of the sample, so the mechanism cannot fail on them. PARTIALLY YES for G7: the arming sequence (half-armed at earlier extremes, fully armed 1113, delivered 1114/1117, stopped at the origin shelf 1118) was a forward test with a stated arming rule that could have fired early and did not, and could have run past the shelf and did not. And the play carries a recorded MISS in its own text (G6 week-2 recovery), which is more honesty than most. One forward confirmation plus one recorded miss is not a measurement base for a block-lean caller.

audit.argument: The play sorts expected magnitude by day-condition: UP-size weekend-gap Monday, storage Thursday and swing-reversal/seam; DOWN-size thin-holiday and non-catalyst chop. The entire support is a CURATED LIST OF DAY NETS on the conditions the play names ('Mon: 1020 +2770, 0929 +1240...; Thu: 0918 -1560, 1002 +1360...'), against a shorter list of small non-catalyst days. There is no counted base rate anywhere in the record. I computed one from the actuals: across G17-G23 (70 scored days, 14 storage Thursdays, 14 Mondays), a storage Thursday exceeds its OWN block's median |day_move| on 8 of 14 = 57%, and a Monday on 8 of 14 = 57%. Thursday's MEAN |move| is 850 against 435-526 for the other day-classes, so the TAIL claim survives - but that mean is carried by two days (0528 +2100, 0709 -2050), and this desk's standing rule forbids leading with a mean. In the CDD block G22 the two storage Thursdays (0625 -60, 0702 0) were the two SMALLEST days of the block against a 575 median, a direct contradiction of the flagship up-size arm. The calibration history is a WIDENING TENT: every time an extreme cleared the band top, the response was a new band (s97_2 winter bands, s98_2 year-end amplifier) and never a falsification - the record's own forward line says 'FORWARD-FAILED in calibration on every block' and keeps the play. And the G11 note raises confidence 0.45 -> 0.5 because the play 'earned the SIDE' on 0119 - a DIRECTION result banked by a play whose declared target is magnitude, on a day it oversized 3x.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: MOSTLY NO. The exemplar lists are selected on the outcome they exist to explain; a big day on a catalyst condition is entered as evidence and a small one is not counted. Two things DID come out the other way and are honestly recorded - the G7 1111 Veterans Day refutation of the thin-holiday down-size (15x under, re-scoped to require no live weather catalyst) and the standing 'the band tops are low' admission. Those are real. But the core up-size claim has never been scored against a base rate, and when I score it, it is 57% - four points better than a coin flip on the split it implies.

plays.trigger: at the OPEN of the session after a give-back (counter-swing) day, reading the prior day's ACTUAL tape
plays.read: prior give-back day's close-vs-extreme recovery + last-hours direction + the underlying swing's big-leg continuation (collapse or intact)
plays.call: EXHAUSTED give-back (close recovered >=~40-50% off the intraday extreme + last-hours counter-tick + swing legs intact) -> next session RESUMES the underlying swing, sized up on a catalyst day. NOT exhausted (close at/near the extreme, last hours extending) -> the give-back CONTINUES. Swing-side legs already collapsed -> stand down (no call). S97.2 ARMS: (ramp) under a LIVE continuous weather catalyst with the swing's big legs intact, a ONE-DAY give-back resumes next session regardless of the close-recovery fraction (the 40-50% band is the no-ramp/autumn read); (depth) at >=~70% swing retrace the R5 capitulation read OUTRANKS the closes-at-low continuation arm - heavy closes at deep retrace precede the bounce. S98.2 SYMMETRIC GENERALIZATION: read EVERY session's close vs its intraday extreme, polarity-relative - a CHAIN-SIDE day closing at its extreme (<~10% recovery) -> chain continues next session; closing >=~35% off the extreme with a late counter-tick -> one-day alternation bounce; a BOUNCE day is never extended in a mature chain regardless of its close (the next print crushes it).
plays.requires: needs_day_N-1_tape
plays.scope: day net (side) of the session AFTER a give-back
plays.caveats: Requires day-N-1 ACTUAL tape - a LIVE-coach / sequential input, honestly unavailable to the one-shot block-blind protocol (this is WHY one-shot direction scored 3/10 while the block lean was right). Thresholds (~40-50% recovery) are descriptive bands, not fitted constants. At >=~75% swing retrace the continue-arm INVERTS - R5 origin-shelf floor takes over (1117->1118). Winter up-swing + G4 evidence; the mirror side (up give-backs inside a down-swing) rests on the collapse filter (0915/0916) - retest. S97.2: n grows to ~13 boundary events; the recovery-fraction thresholds are subordinate to the ramp and depth arms in winter. G9 CAVEAT (load-bearing): the boundary read is POLARITY-RELATIVE - after a chain flip (first violent counter day off a parabolic crest, 1208 -2730) 'resume' means resume the NEW swing's direction. The blind run misapplied it up-side 3x (1212/1215/1222). S98.2: symmetric close-vs-extreme read confirmed on the G9 down-chain (7/8 boundaries); the bounce-day override (never extend, print crushes) is the down-chain asymmetry vs autumn up-chain give-backs that DID continue (1002->1003, 1114->1117) - polarity + print-schedule context decides, retest. S99.2: the symmetric read is CHAIN-SIDE-days-only (0105), and in bleed the post-crash continue arm is overridden by B1 (pause) unless a print day follows.
plays.falsifier: None written; the play has an empty falsifier field despite six arms. TWO ARE AVAILABLE. (1) For the flow-absorption arm, the one I ran: count fires of bp>=0.62 AND sb<=0.45 across served sessions and check the next-session direction. Result: 3 of 60 fires in g18-g23, all on <=6 big prints, 1 right and 2 wrong; adding the only thick-tape fire in the corpus (g16 0408, -450 against a called turn) makes it 1-of-4. (2) For the primary arm, the falsifier must be stated in refine terms since the blind cannot see it: on the refine's realized tape, classify each give-back day's close-recovery fraction BEFORE reading the next day, and require the resume/continue call to beat a coin flip on >= 10 boundary events not used in derivation. Nothing in the corpus has ever done that.

audit.argument: A real mechanism is argued: a counter-swing (give-back) that exhausts lets the underlying swing resume, one that does not exhaust continues. The support is a very large per-event narrative in which the close-recovery fraction and the outcome are read together, day by day, and the play itself concedes the parameters were read off those outcomes - 'Thresholds (~40-50% recovery) are descriptive bands, not fitted constants.' EVERY COUNTEREXAMPLE PRODUCED A NEW ARM RATHER THAN A REFUTATION, six times: S97.2 added a ramp arm and a depth arm; G9 added polarity-relativity after the blind misapplied it up-side three times; S98.2 added a bounce-never-extends asymmetry; S99.2 added chain-side-days-only plus a bleed override; S102.2 added the flow-absorption arm. THE RECORD CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON ONE DAY: forward_evidence calls G11 0129 'a clean forward hit' (resume called, +1,480 actual) while legacy_notes.g11_note says the play 'fired twice, both directions missed - 0126 -620a vs +500g and 0129 +1480a vs -1800g'. Both cannot be true of the same fire; the resolution is that the 'forward hit' is a refine-time re-application with the outcome visible, and the field does not say so. AVAILABILITY: the primary close-vs-extreme arm needs day-N-1 realized price and is stood down by construction in every modern blind - I verified explicit stand-downs in grp22_B_20260622, grp22_B_20260629, grp22_D_20260625 and grp23_C_20260707 - and it appears in NO refine posterior for g19-g23. So the primary arm has zero evaluations anywhere in the modern corpus. I THEREFORE MEASURED THE ONE BLIND-AVAILABLE ARM, the S102.2 flow-absorption turn (big_print_b_share >= ~0.62 AND session_b_share <= ~0.45), across all 60 served sessions of g18-g23: it fires 3 times, on 1, 6 and 2 big prints. Every fire is a degenerate thin-tape reading of exactly the kind flow.big_print_bshare_thin_tape_guard exists to stand down. On well-sampled tape (big_prints_n >= 20) it is 0 of ~50 - the 0.62 bar sits above the entire thick-tape distribution in six blocks. TO THE PLAY'S CREDIT, ITS DERIVATION REPRODUCES EXACTLY: grp15_state.json serves the 0317 session under key 20260318 at big_print_b_share 0.643 / session_b_share 0.413 (the founding fire, +1,900), and all four named non-fires reproduce to three decimals (0319 0.593, 0322 0.542, 0324 0.373, 0325 0.174). But the founding fire itself sits on 14 big prints, inside the thin quartile.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The narrative evidence, NO. Once a break can be reclassified into a new arm - ramp, depth, polarity, bleed, chain-side-only - no day can refute the play, and the record is a history of exactly that reclassification. The G11 entry shows the mechanism operating in miniature: two recorded direction misses were re-attributed to 'a known-degraded input, not a test of the read with tape.' MY ARM-LEVEL MEASUREMENT, YES, and it could easily have returned a bar that splits days sensibly; instead it returned 3 fires in 60 sessions, all degenerate.

plays.read: sessions since the swing turned + yesterday's close vs the running extreme
plays.call: YOUNG swing (<=3 sessions since the turn): extensions can CHAIN - do not fade strength. MATURE swing (>=4 sessions): a material fresh extreme close is NOT followed by a consecutive extension - forecast a give-back/hold session, then apply R1 to the give-back's own close for the resume/continue call. A post-VIOLENT-resumption session is a HOLD (probes fail, net ~0): 0924 +50 after 0923; 1112 +100 after 1111.

G11 0121 is the first kind. A serviceable written form: over a block, count material-fresh-extreme closes and score the next session; two consecutive extensions in a mature chain more than ~30 pct of the time retires the rhythm.

legacy_notes.conditions_note: THE BARS ARE REAL AND BOTH OPERANDS ARE UNSERVED. The trigger carries two genuine numeric bars - swing AGE (<=3 young / >=4 mature, counted in sessions since the swing turned) and materiality of '>= ~$300 beyond the prior extreme close'. Neither quantity exists in the vocabulary. There is no swing-age or chain-age path (squeeze_watch.sessions_since_prompt_expiry counts sessions since a CONTRACT expiry, a different clock; the cot/storage/steo *.age_days fields are data staleness), and no close-versus-running-extreme path. vol_regime.n0_prev_net cannot carry the $300 bar: it is a session NET, not a close measured against the running extreme, and in the blind state it is frozen at the anchor vintage and constant across the block. The play's health field says the same from the other side - C stands it down on G20 0525/0603, G22 0624/0630/0701 and G23 0707 because 'chain age and cum-from-anchor are price content the mask removes'. NOTE ON THE ONE SERVED-LOOKING ARM: the s101_6_expiry_day_form sub-arm in legacy_notes turns on expiry proximity (served as flow_calendar.days_to_futures_expiry / days_to_opex) and on stranded premium (contract_structure.calendar_front_next_spread). I deliberately did not curate it: no threshold is written for 'stranded premium absent' - E-0626 judged -0.043 to be absent by eye - and the arm's own brain_action assigns it to structure.squeeze_unwind, not to this play's trigger. Curating it would be inventing a bar and attaching it to the wrong play.

audit.argument: A demand-led swing sequences: a mature swing (age >= 4) cannot post a consecutive fresh cum-extreme, so a material fresh extreme close is followed by a give-back or hold, then R1 is applied to the give-back's own close for the resume call; a young swing (<= 3 sessions) chains and must not be faded. The mechanism is a real one - a positioning cycle needs a session to reload - and the play states its own boundary as descriptive rather than sharp, names the swing-side asymmetry (supply-led G3 trended instead of alternating), and hands magnitude to other plays rather than inventing one. The evidence is unusually thick and is COUNTED, not narrated: G7 5/5 with dated pairs and dollar moves; young-chain counterexamples listed; a materiality rule derived from a case it would otherwise have gotten wrong (1112 +100 closed INSIDE 1111's range, so not a material extreme, so 1113 extended); G9 post-flip alternation; G10 bounce-never-extended n=4; and G11 scored per-event at 4 fires, 2 on side, with confidence lowered 0.6 -> 0.55 in consequence.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: Yes, repeatedly, and it did. The G11 tally reproduces exactly from the committed score file - 0120 +700g/+1930a HIT, 0128 -1000g/-400a HIT, 0121 -800g against +3820a MISS, 0127 +300g/-260a MISS - i.e. the play's strongest structural call of that week failed and was written up as a failure with a diagnosed cause (the polarity input, not the rhythm). C-0715 then contradicted the YOUNG-swing limb on G23 0708 in a refine posterior and explicitly declined to propose on it at n=1. That is a rule that has been allowed to lose.

plays.trigger: sizing a running give-back / calling its stabilization day
plays.read: retrace fraction of the swing + the swing's origin/consolidation shelf price
plays.call: A terminal give-back runs toward the swing's ORIGIN shelf and stabilizes there (give-back-not-reversal). At >=~75% retrace, INVERT the R1 closes-at-low read: a capitulation close at the stretched extreme precedes the BOUNCE/stabilization, not more continuation.

plays.caveats: The >=75% threshold is soft (n=4); the shelf is a zone, not a tick. Distinguish mid-swing give-backs (R1 governs) from move-terminal stretches (this play governs). A shelf BREAK would falsify the give-back-not-reversal frame for that swing - treat as a live stop condition. S97.2: threshold softened to >=~70% (1125 at 72% fired); still a zone, not a tick. S98.2 VOID-CONDITION: after a confirmed parabolic polarity flip the shelf BREAKS (1211 through the 4.367 origin) - the break confirms reversal-not-give-back; only NON-parabolic give-backs respect the shelf (G7). n=1 break vs n=5 holds, condition = the parabolic arm.

That is concrete and it has already fired once (1211). The newer validated/unvalidated arm needs its own: an unvalidated leg that does NOT retrace to its origin.

legacy_notes.conditions_note: THE BAR IS REAL AND BOTH OPERANDS ARE UNSERVED. The bar is a retrace FRACTION of the swing (>=~75%, softened to >=~70%) measured against the swing's ORIGIN SHELF PRICE. Neither is in the vocabulary: no retrace fraction, no cum-from-anchor, no swing-origin level. The vocabulary does now serve price LEVELS - options_surface.months[i].top5_oi_strikes[j].strike and oi_weighted_strike, newly visible as indexed paths - and I rejected them explicitly: an open-interest pin strike is a different level from the price a swing launched off, and substituting one for the other is precisely the 'the name looked right' failure this curation exists to prevent. The play itself concedes the reference is not even a single number ('the shelf is a zone, not a tick'). Its health field confirms the play is refine-only on the current architecture, and records that the one time a blind did fire it (0227) it fired at a shelf price had already broken through.

audit.argument: MECHANISM: a terminal give-back runs back toward the price level where the swing began and stabilizes there, because below that shelf price is no longer priced by the driver that produced the swing. The squeeze form spells the mechanism out fully - post-expiry appreciation has no delivery anchor and no sponsor, so it unwinds to where the pull began and stops. MEASUREMENT, and this is the strongest instance record in the batch: five per-event instances with dates and dollar outcomes, every one of which I recomputed from the committed continuous series rather than trusting the brain. 0922 close 2.801 -> 0923 2.864 = +630 (brain says +610). 1016 2.925 -> 1017 3.000 = +750 (brain +740). 1117 4.339 -> 1118 4.366 = +270 (brain +270) and the brain names the shelf as the 4.32-4.34 zone, which the 4.339 close sits ON. 1029 3.803 -> 1030 4.062 = +2590 (brain +2580). 1125 4.474 -> 1126 4.611 = +1370 (brain +1360). THE PLAY THEN RECORDS ITS OWN FALSIFICATION AND SCOPES IT: 1211 broke through the 4.367 origin (1210 4.616 -> 1211 4.220) and the brain converts that into a VOID CONDITION - after a confirmed parabolic polarity flip the shelf breaks and the break confirms reversal-not-give-back. n=1 break against n=5 holds, and the discriminator (squeeze form holds / weather-parabola form breaks) is named rather than the tent widened. A play that recorded its own counterexample and derived a condition from it is not resting on outcome credit.
audit.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, demonstrably - it DID come out the other way once and the record says so. 1117 could have kept falling through 4.32 and did not; 1211 did fall through 4.367 and was recorded as a void rather than explained away. The added S110 arm (a covering leg retraces in full to its origin only if no phase was validated by aligned flow) is weaker: n=2 clean on the two days its author owned, with 0601 a declared partial where the origin did NOT hold as a floor, and both measured in refine round 2 with the outcome known.

plays.trigger: an armed turn/resume boundary (R1/R5) with a scheduled catalyst (storage print, forecast HDD peak) 1-3 sessions ahead
plays.read: is a CONTINUOUS catalyst live? (a hard_heat/cold ramp visible and updating in the weather models) vs discrete-only (shoulder season, the print is the info event)
plays.call: LIVE continuous catalyst -> the armed resume fires the NEXT session, FRONT-RUNNING the scheduled event; the event day itself then obeys the chain (usually post-violent give-back / sell-the-news). NO live ramp -> the resume WAITS and the scheduled catalyst delivers it. Never calendar-anchor a resume to the catalyst day when a ramp is live. S98.2 RISING-RAMP ARM: when the forward HDD stream is still RISING through and beyond the print day, the front-run runs THROUGH the print (intraday morning give-back, catalyst wins the close: 1204 +1100); the post-violent give-back form needs the ramp crested at/before the print (1120, 1202, 1002). POST-FLIP: cold-delivery days FAIL (1215 -1560 on HDD 32.5; 1230 spike-faded on HDD 30.1) - never extend a delivery day against the chain. S99.2 ARBITER ARM: the first scheduled print after an armed turn is the turn's ARBITER - counter-side delivery confirms (0925, 1030), chain-side delivery refutes (0109 sold the bullish draw = the false flip refuted). Front-running remains WITH-chain-resume-only; a flip confirm must print first (C3).
plays.requires: open_time_only
plays.scope: timing (which session an armed turn/resume fires on)
plays.caveats: Mechanism: weather models are a continuous information stream (2x daily updates) - when live they dominate timing and the discrete event only adds magnitude/liquidity; in a discrete-only regime the print IS the information event. n=2 fired (G7, G8) vs n=2 waited (G3/4, G6) - spanning but thin; the decisive test is the next winter armed-turn near a print. In one-shot mode this rule sets the PRIOR (front-run under a ramp); only day-N-1 tape confirms the chain phase. G10 CAVEAT: NEVER front-run a POLARITY FLIP (0108). Front-running is for resumes WITH the chain; a flip needs its band-breaking confirm to PRINT first.
plays.falsifier: The play carries NO falsifier field, though its caveats name a decisive test in prose ('the decisive test is the next winter armed-turn near a print'). What it actually needs first is a SERVED DEFINITION of ramp-live - pick the quantity and the bar - because until then the condition is not falsifiable, only arguable. Once defined: front-runs under a live ramp must beat the base rate of the pre-print session, measured on the intraday window and not on the day net (this is the exact defect s103.6 had to retract on D's pre-print generator).

health.can_change_state: This is the play's real defect and it is worse than a degenerate bar. The trigger has TWO limbs. The calendar limb (a scheduled catalyst 1-3 sessions ahead, served as flow_calendar.days_to_next_eia_release) is live and splits days cleanly. The ramp-live limb has NO SERVED DEFINITION, and the two natural readings of the same served object disagree in SIGN on the same day (20260624: horizon-0 forecast_run_delta_cdd -0.011 vs h1 d_gw_cdd +0.787). Under the h1 reading it is a constant, positive 20/20 across two groups - it cannot gate. Under the level reading it is whatever the reader says. So the limb either cannot change state or changes state by reader choice, and the corpus contains one specialist doing both inside one block.
