seasonal_salience_slider.provenance: Greg, desk doctrine, paraphrased faithfully: 'the scoring weights slide through the year - weather is a lot more important in winter and summer than fall and spring.'
seasonal_salience_slider.text: (a) Input-family importance is SEASONAL, not fixed: WEATHER (MOS stream, cycles, freeze risk, HDD/CDD) carries maximum weight in DEEP WINTER and SUMMER (heating/cooling demand regimes) and fades through FALL and SPRING shoulders; in shoulders the weight shifts toward FLOWS and MAINTENANCE SEASON (nuclear refuel clusters, pipeline work, LNG turnarounds - the nuclear_outages/grid_stack family), storage-TRAJECTORY (the injection/withdrawal season turn), and structure/positioning. (b) HONESTY: the walk's evidence to date is winter-only - the brain's weather-heavy rule set is winter-calibrated BY CIRCUMSTANCE and should be EXPECTED to age as the walk exits winter (G14+ into March/April = the spring shoulder + maintenance season + the injection-season turn). A rule fading in the shoulder is the slider working, not the rule failing - but that judgment requires this slider to be stated. (c) TIE-INS: the G6 lesson (HDD beats surplus at the autumn->winter transition) is the slider's first recorded instance; regime_scope already names warm-season vs winter thinness; the day-class layer is ORTHOGONAL (class first, then seasonal salience inside the class); magnitude bands stay regime/condition-scoped exactly as they are. (d) FORWARD CONSEQUENCE: G14 opens the walk's first shoulder-season blocks - the slider's first forward test; at each block open the agent reads the seasonal position explicitly (calendar + storage phase + HDD/CDD levels) and records which family it weights and why, per-event.
seasonal_salience_slider.forward_evidence: NONE - doctrine input this pass; G14 is the designed first test.

s102_1_operational_form.S1_demand_base_switch: NEAR-window NORMALS base (climo, zero forecast noise) >=~21 gw-HDD: weather-trajectory authority live BOTH signs, chain-conditioned as the winter brain holds. <=~20: warm-cut trajectory authority VOID for gaps, day-sides and block leans (the inversion ladder: wk1 cut mass vs realized move - g12 base 20-30: -10.4gw -> -10,110; g10: -11.7 -> -2,960; g13: -8.9 -> -740; g7 base 9-15: -13.8 -> +2,100; g14 base 7-20: -16.3 -> +3,250. Monotone in base, zero exceptions, symmetric across both shoulders). Boundary 20.6/21.2 at the walk's resolution, not tuned.
s102_1_operational_form.S2_shock_exception: Cold ADDS price on both sides of S1 (below-boundary 4/4: 1106, 1109, 0305, 0311). In shoulder count the FULL window incl. D+5..D+7. Warm cuts touching a LIVE cold event <=2 sessions old are event-trims and retain authority (0313 -1010).
s102_1_operational_form.S3_ownership_handoff: S1-void: block-lean/gap ownership passes to storage-TRAJECTORY (consensus-implied vs-5yr for the NEXT print, anchor-computable - NOT the last print's level, which pointed wrong in G14 wk1), maintenance-FLOWS (nuclear chg-7d sign/size bracketed the entire G14 rally: onset at ramp-max +4.1GW/7d, fade the day it flipped negative), and POSITIONING as amplifier. In S1-void state weather may own gaps ONLY on the S2 add class, never cuts.
s102_1_operational_form.not_covered: Summer/CDD mirror unmeasured (no CDD>3 in the walk); G6-and-earlier (no MOS store); whether ~21 is seasonally stationary (one winter).
s102_1_operational_form.forward_evidence: G14 = the first shoulder test: S1-void reads explain 5/5 week-1 days the weather batches got 2/5; the two gap ownership misses are exactly the calls S3's line removes. G15+ per-event forward tests designed (refine C).

seasonal_salience_slider.g15_forward_evidence: S1/S2/S3 FORWARD-CONFIRMED AT THE REGIME LEVEL (first test beyond G14): the blind read S1 VOID both weeks (near-normals base ~17 falling to ~14 gw < 21) and handed the block leans to S3 storage-trajectory (the 0319 print +59 loose = bearish wk1; the 0326 -43 tight = bullish wk2) + maintenance-flows (nuclear ramp +5.6GW/7d = the wk2 amplifier) + positioning-as-amplifier - and the block direction was RIGHT. The slider MACHINERY worked forward; what it does NOT yet calibrate is MAGNITUDE (the -3490-vs-600 oversizing = the S103 refine's core question: are shoulder give-back BANDS shallower than winter, or is it a few specific days). Open-conditions used as intended: tape_conditions drove the 0324 extension, the 0325 alternation, and the 0317/0318 big-print-buy divergences (store-mix caveat 0316-0319 honored).

body.rule: EXACTLY ONE rule owns a decision node at any time - never two weighed against each other. While a refined rule is in its one-block forward probation, the INCUMBENT rule owns the blind node outright (probation is not co-ownership). The moment the refined rule earns forward evidence, ownership HANDS OFF completely: the superseded rule retires from the decision tree and survives ONLY as (a) a cautionary instance - how not to do it, with its named failure days - and (b) a watch-trigger where it reminds the agent to look at something the new rule does not surface. It is never again a weighted alternative.

body.rule: Every one-shot blind group run STARTS FROM A FRESH SESSION: the orchestrator that spawns the blind agent must carry nothing beyond the drop-in box, the current brain, and decision_state. An orchestrator that has spent its session building feeds, reading tapes, or measuring stores that overlap the group's window is CONTAMINATED CONTEXT for refereeing a holdout - even though the blind agent itself receives only brain + decision_state, the referee's knowledge shapes spawning, adjudication and scoring (the G11 caveat: 'the orchestrator had seen this block's price path before the blind agent was spawned... a weaker holdout, weighted accordingly'). Build sessions END with the close-out ritual; blind runs OPEN the next session.

body.rule: Gap and net remain separately scored events; what changes is that OWNERSHIP is explicit and the reporting cannot hide one behind the other. (1) DECLARE: every forecast of a block-opening or Sunday reopen gap must carry gap_owner in {anchor_structural, weekend_cycle_weather, chain_drift} declared AT THE ANCHOR/prior close, plus the band class used. (2) SCORE: the scorecard's day row carries gap_dir_ok AND gap_class_ok (realized gap inside the declared band, tail declared = miss with named tail) at EQUAL RANK with net_dir_ok; reopen days additionally carry day_move_dir_ok (sign of gap+net) - the headline hit/miss for a reopen day is the day_move composite, so 0201 reads MISS (+150g vs -7590a day move) with the net sub-score a hit, never the reverse. (3) ATTRIBUTE: when the realized gap's driver class differs from the declared owner, the OWNERSHIP call is scored as the miss (a new ownership_ok flag) - that is the exact error 0201 exposes (blind declared weather-priced; the driver was structural). (4) DRIFT attribution names gap residual separately from net residual per day, as g12_score already does numerically - the change is the headline convention.
body.g13_0215_procedure: At the 0213 anchor (close 3.084 on instrument 996/April): FIRST declare the 0215 gap owner. Structural check: March (NGH26) expiry Feb 25 falls INSIDE G13 and squeeze_watch's day-count is <=7 from 0213 - read the March-April spread's level and 3d change at the anchor (0212 vintage: +0.137): positive-AND-widening -> anchor_structural owner, squeeze doctrine (bands void on the squeeze leg; the walk instrument is April, once-removed - the G12 handoff note stands); flat/narrowing (the G12-observed state: collapsed from +0.336 to ~+0.09-0.16 post-unwind) -> no structural owner. THEN the weekend cycle: fresh/accelerating shot at D+2..D+6 -> weather owner with the fresh band at the shot's sign; nothing fresh -> chain_drift owner: 0213 closed -160 mid-range (NOT at a chain extreme), so the drift band is the priced stub +-200..400 at chain sign, NOT the -600..-1600 continuation class (that class requires a prior close AT its extreme). Score 0215 per (2)-(3): gap_dir, gap_class, ownership, then the Sunday session net as its own event, then day_move composite as the headline.

b_monday_toolbag.phase_structure: Four named phases: (1) SUNDAY REOPEN GAP - electronic, prices the weekend per the gap owner; (2) overnight/Asia-Europe drift - thin; (3) THE CATCH-UP WINDOW ~06-10 ET (Greg: 7-10) - human desks reprice/judge the weekend move; (4) post-10 ET - the day's chain behavior proper owns the close.
b_monday_toolbag.ownership: The OPEN belongs to the weekend toolbag (gap owner). The CATCH-UP WINDOW belongs to R3's reaction verdict - this is the COMPOSITION Greg asked for: R3's 'Monday is the reaction' is not spread over the day, it is CONCENTRATED 06-10 ET, where the desk either FADES/repositions the electronic overnight or RATIFIES it into delivery. The CLOSE belongs to the chain state (ordinary day-net rules).

b_monday_toolbag.thin_holiday_monday: Holiday Mondays have NO catch-up desks: the window is DEFERRED to Tuesday. Per-event: 1013 Columbus quiet -300 (no catalyst, hold); 0119 MLK +550 after the +2100 gap consumed the catalyst (no curve data - G11 gap); 1124-adjacent and 1127 Thanksgiving support thin=damper on hold days, amplifier only on DELIVERY days (1111, 1128). Rule form: on a holiday Monday the weekend REACTION spreads across Mon-Tue; forecast the reaction as a two-session read.

(2) THE FRIDAY CLOSE IS THE WEEKEND ANCHOR: its close-vs-extreme position and state vintage feed the entire weekend toolbag (0130 at-extreme -> dead-sponsor gap; 0206 at-low -> chain-drift gap) - Friday's last hours are the anchor-quality input, which is a REASON Friday reads matter beyond Friday. (3) Chain rules still APPLY intraday Friday - no Friday damper exists in the walk: 1205 +2440 crest, 1128 +2340 melt-up, 0109 -2760 print crash, 0130 +5020 all printed ON Fridays.

Per-event: squaring appears when the day is STRETCHED COUNTER TO the running chain or terminal (1205), never against a live delivery. n=2 vs n=2 - THIN, recorded as a lean, not a band.

addendum_holiday_doctrine.provenance: Greg, final input pre-merge (faithful): 'holidays can only be scored against that holiday historically. unfortunately he won't have that but it will probably look closer to a Sun than Mon.'
addendum_holiday_doctrine.a_holiday_day_class: HOLIDAY sessions are their OWN day-class, comparable only to the SAME holiday in prior years - never to generic Mondays/weekdays.
addendum_holiday_doctrine.b_named_structural_gap: The walk has NO prior-year holiday history (one winter of data). This is a NAMED structural gap - never proxy it silently with weekday evidence.
addendum_holiday_doctrine.c_default_prior: Absent same-holiday history, the DEFAULT PRIOR for a holiday session is the SUNDAY-LIKE read: thin tape, state-reads-only, drift bands, rhythm tools VOID - the Sunday-session read set of (a), NOT the Monday toolbag. A holiday Monday reads closer to a Sunday than a Monday.
addendum_holiday_doctrine.d_0216_revised: 0216 Presidents Day REVISED under (c): 0216 = SUNDAY-LIKE session - thin drift band (-600..+700), weekend-bag state reads only, rhythm/alternation/catch-up tools void; the catch-up window defers to 0217's 06-10 ET window (two-session R3 reaction read unchanged). In-walk evidence, both instances consistent with the Sunday-like prior: 1013 Columbus -300 (quiet hold), 0119 MLK +550 after the +2100 gap consumed the catalyst - small nets post-gap-consumption. The thin-amplifier exception (1111, 1128) remains conditional on a LIVE delivery catalyst and is itself holiday-class evidence, n=2.
addendum_holiday_doctrine.multi_year_fix: EVENTUAL SCORER: as the walk extends and live-forward accrues, same-holiday history becomes buildable - Presidents Day 2027 scores against Presidents Day 2026, etc. Until then every holiday call carries the Sunday-like-prior tag and the named gap.
addendum_holiday_doctrine.extended_weekend_note: GREG (2026-07-21): "the whole weekend if it's on a Mon might look unique." A HOLIDAY-EXTENDED WEEKEND (3-day closure: Fri close -> holiday Mon, real desk flow returning Tuesday) is flagged as potentially its OWN sub-class of the weekend class, not a normal weekend plus a holiday: one extra day of information accrues (additional model cycles, longer decay window for any structural premium), the closure spans TWO thin sessions (Sunday + holiday Monday) before desks return, and the catch-up window lands Tuesday 06-10 ET. Comparable ideally only to the SAME holiday weekend historically - the same-holiday scoring rule extends to the whole closure, and the same named history gap applies. body.load_bearing_principle: The OLD (blind) prediction framework STAYS the CORE forecasting model. L1+trades+MBO is NOT a replacement predictor - it is a CAUSAL REFINEMENT LAYER that decides whether the immutable blind is still valid as the session unfolds. The refined output is a POSTERIOR UPDATE OF THE IMMUTABLE BLIND, never a new forecast from scratch. Do not replace a working predictor with a reactive order-flow model.
pieces_in_order: 1 IMMUTABLE BLIND = the starting map (direction, magnitude, timing, turns, daily path; pre-cutoff info only). Never rewritten.

2 FRIDAY ANCHOR = the starting market state (final traded hour before the block: price, dir, volume, signed flow, activity, efficiency, contract identity, queue). First Sunday update is read RELATIVE to this.
3 NORMALIZED L1+TRADES+DEFINITIONS+MBO = ONE chronological stream feeding ONE feature engine. None predict independently.
4 NGLiveOperator + FEATURE STATES = events -> behavior, emitted ONLY at valid completed-event boundaries. Never chase ticks or react to incomplete books.
5 SESSION SPECIALISTS = interpret the SAME feature state by session structure (a feature means different things Sunday vs Tue-core vs EIA-Thu vs expiry/roll-Fri).
6 COORDINATOR = SELECTS the specialist matching the day+state; NEVER averages opposing forecasts; records which, why, dissent, why the alternative was rejected.

7 POSTERIOR REFINEMENT = starts from the blind and adjusts ONLY when causal evidence is MATERIAL (confirm / reduce confidence / delay / resize / identify a turn / flip continuation-vs-reversal / stand down). Emits SEPARATE outputs, not one vague call.

8 DATA QUALITY / STAND-DOWN = controls authority. MBO book-based conclusions require a trustworthy reconstructed book. Book unreliable but trades valid -> fall back to trade-flow+L1 and LABEL it. Weak data must never create false precision.

9 SCORING = score blind vs refined SEPARATELY; direction alone insufficient - measure magnitude, path, onset, turns, MFE, MAE, trend-vs-chop, confidence calibration. Distinguishes genuine improvement from merely REACTING after the move.
10 LESSON PROPOSALS = propose mechanisms with supporting events, counterexamples, scope, n, confidence, forward validation. Never auto-rewrite the brain.
body.goal: Preserve what the old framework did well; use the new data to improve TIMING, MAGNITUDE, TURNS, and CONFIDENCE - not to replace it.

body.discriminator_that_works: signed-flow-vs-price CONVICTION on the phase leg: flow_conviction = sign(signed_flow)*sign(price_change) (or corr) per phase. ALIGNED delivers the band; NEGATIVE-under-rising = absorption/covering -> reversal/round-trip. This ONE derived feature does the discrimination that onset_dir / absorb-flag / print-direction CANNOT (those were identical on 0319 and 0326 yet resolved oppositely).
body.direction_source_rule: Direction stays with the D-1 trade tilt (prior-session big_print_b_share / session_b_share) that the blind already consumes. Gate 1-min imb_flow OUT of the direction decision entirely; use MBO only for TURN and ABSORPTION confirmation. imb_flow flips faster than its own autocorrelation at 30-min grain - a sampling artifact, not signal.
body.anticipation_vs_confirmation: The 0318 anticipatory signal (bid-level build near the low) was already in the D-1 trades the open-conditions blind saw. MBO's honest role on 0318 was CONFIRMATION, not anticipation. Scored as improved-vs-reacted: the turn magnitude tail (+1900 actual) was partly reactive; the confirmed base was +1500.
engine_change_requests: Emit ONE session-level data-quality verdict (book_trustworthy bit = execution_authority AND conviction>=floor AND book_complete) + only material transition bars, NOT 150+ repeated stand-down rows.
Phase-first not tick-first: feed the specialist the phase table + session turns as the PRIMARY object; demote the minute-grain series to a diagnostic.
Print-anchored windows on EIA-Thu: reset phases at the 10:30 ET print (pre-print / delivery / post-delivery), not volume-based boundaries that straddle the print.

Roll seam as a first-class engine object: a leg_map (raw_symbol per date, NGJ26 pre-roll / NGK26 post-roll, not NG.n.0) + an explicit seam_event traded=false so overnight_gap is forced to 0 and the offset is scoring-only.

he24_to_he1_handoff_spec.principle: The day-boundary handoff carries STATE, never the day-net number. Each specialist starts from the prior day's MARKET CONDITION so the block is one continuous path, not siloed guesses.

he24_to_he1_handoff_spec.turn_ownership: A turn firing in the overnight HE24->HE1 seam belongs to the boundary: whoever owns the day the turn REALIZES into inherits it, but sizes it using the PRIOR day's exhaustion-state flag (so 0318 doesn't compound a possibly-overshot tail).

A weekend that also carries a contract roll passes the leg change as never-traded.

THE_MODEL.one_line: Only GAS regulates to load. Everything else is either a FORCING set outside the power market, or a LEVEL moving on a timescale longer than a session.
THE_MODEL.forcings_must_run_zero_fuel_cost: WIND, SOLAR, HYDRO. Must-run, taking whatever the resource gives, and NONE is ever curtailed for ECONOMICS - Greg: 'hydro is never curtailed for econ. It's essentially free so as long as there's no river issues it's going.' Output is set OUTSIDE the power market: wind and solar by weather, hydro by WATER MANAGEMENT (flood control, reservoir level, irrigation calls, water rights, minimum flows, discharge temperature). A price signal moves none of them.
THE_MODEL.levels_baseload: NUCLEAR and COAL. Committed and running; they do not ramp to meet a demand spike. Coal is cheaper than gas, which is why gas does not displace it in dispatch. Both move on OUTAGE, RETIREMENT and seasonal-COMMITMENT timescales - weeks to years - never on the day-ahead timescale a session forecast lives on.
THE_MODEL.the_regulator: GAS, and only gas. gas_burn = load - wind - solar - hydro - nuclear - coal. As the sole regulator it absorbs the load swing AND every forcing's swing, at full size, in whichever direction they go. A miss in any other term lands entirely on gas.

body.WHY_0629_WAS_STRUCTURAL_NOT_UNLUCKY: gw_cdd rose 10.0 -> 14.8 exactly as forecast and gas burn FELL 4.2 Bcf/d because wind rose 62%. Coal did not move; gas took the whole swing. MEASURED S112: forward LOAD is served (grid_stack.bas.*.demand_forecast_mwh, all seven BAs, all-modern) and the whole weather_forecast family is forward - but wind and solar are REALIZED ONLY, with no forward field in any block. So NET LOAD IS UNCOMPUTABLE FORWARD: we hold one half of it. Realized wind cannot fix a forward call because on a forecast day the realized value does not exist yet. Registry G-4.
body.HYDRO_THE_WATER_TO_OUTPUT_CURVE_IS_AN_IN:
Output rises with runoff UP TO A POINT, then FALLS. The falling limb is neither economic nor discretionary: past a river stage the Army Corps of Engineers directs operators to OPEN THE GATES so the river does not overtop its banks, and that water goes through the SPILLWAY INSTEAD OF THE TURBINES - bypassing generation while water is at its most abundant.

SO BOTH TAILS ARE BULLISH GAS, for opposite physical reasons: EXTREME HIGH WATER (spill, spring) and LOW WATER (drawdown, irrigation, minimum flows, summer). The bearish-gas case is the MIDDLE.

THE SEASONS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC IN CONSEQUENCE, which is Greg's point: the summer shortfall coincides with PEAK LOAD, so the gap lands on gas at the worst moment. Spring 'not so much'; summer 'really matters'.
body.THE_D23_D28_WARNING_THIS_CARRIES: A single bar on water level or runoff WILL BE WRONG IN ONE TAIL, because the same low-hydro reading is produced by two opposite states of the world. The LEVEL cannot carry the sign; the STATE must. Clearest case on the desk of the value-versus-shape problem, and a direct warning for D32 analog retrieval: a match keyed on hydro OUTPUT alone would pair a high-water spring day with a low-water summer day and call them the same shape.
body.MEASURED_ON_OUR_OWN_STATES:
119 scored days, Feb-Jul 2026, using the unaccounted slice (total_gen_mwh minus coal + nuclear + gas + wind + solar) as a hydro proxy. Monthly Feb->Jul: 8.24 / 9.40 / 9.33 / 8.63 / 7.78 / 7.04 percent of US48 generation, while gas share rises 34.8% -> 42.2%. The 9.40 -> 7.04 March-to-July fall is about 290,000 MWh/day, roughly 2.0-2.3 Bcf/d if gas fills it at 7-8 MMBtu/MWh - the same order as the 4.2 Bcf/d 0629 wind event.

CAVEATS carried with the number: the residual is hydro PLUS oil, biomass and other; summer gas share also rises on cooling load independently; and the window holds ONE spring, so it says nothing either way about a high-water spill event. Co-movement in the stated direction, NOT an isolated causal estimate - enough to justify serving the field and instrumenting SUMMER first, not enough to write a bar on.
body.THE_SERVED_STATE_TODAY_AND_ITS_HOLES:
SERVED, READ BY NOBODY: coal_mwh (US48 + 6 BAs) referenced by ZERO plays with ZERO conditions; nuclear_mwh ZERO; wind_mwh and solar_mwh by exactly ONE play each - weather.burn_conversion_gate, which is RETIRED. Three stack terms have no reader and the fourth's only reader is dead (A-15).

HYDRO - CORRECTED S112, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. My first read said 'not served at all'. It is not served, but it IS STORED, back to 2019-01-01, and has been the whole time. grid_stack.py sets no fueltype facet, so the pull returns every fuel EIA publishes and stores each under gen_mwh[fueltype]; the serving read _ba_read then hand-picks five - NG, SUN, WND, COL, NUC - and drops the rest. EIA-930's hydro code is WAT. The 6.7-7.6% of US48 generation I measured as 'unnamed' is the proof: total_gen_mwh sums ALL fuels, so that gap exists precisely BECAUSE WAT, OIL and OTH are in the store, counted in the denominator, unnamed in the numerator.

SO THE DISEASE IS NOT A MISSING FEED, IT IS A HAND-MAINTAINED COPY LIST - the third time this desk has paid for that exact shape. S107: big_print_b_share size-weighted computed then omitted from the emit list, the count-based one shadowing it under the same name. S109: session_b_share, the one b_share field missing from _tape_enrich's copy list, invisible for as long as the other path happened to be right. Now: the whole hydro fleet, seven years of it, behind a five-element list in a serving function. Correct data does not have to be absent to be useless.

STILL ABSENT: any FORWARD wind or solar (G-4). Any FORWARD nuclear planned-outage schedule; only realized nuclear_outages.* (A-17). Any river-stage or spill indicator (A-16/A-18).

D12: a feed with no named consumer is a staging defect, not a neutral fact. 0629 is what that costs.
body.WHAT_TO_INGEST_AND_HOW_TO_SCOPE_IT:
COAL - not the price, the GENERATION: 'we really only need to know how much of the coal gen is running', already served. The prompt-quarter price accrual (G-11) is a slow structural LEVEL, sticky, never a weekly signal. The published coal-to-gas switching bands are a COMMITMENT-horizon signal about which units get committed over weeks and months, NOT a daily dispatch signal.

HYDRO - TWO inputs, not one: generation from EIA-930 (a field on a feed we already pull) AND a river-stage or spill indicator to separate the tails (USACE, USGS, free). Without the second the first cannot carry a sign.

NUCLEAR and COAL - what is wanted is the forward RETIREMENT and PLANNED-OUTAGE CALENDAR, dated ahead, the one information class the horizon research says survives past the 5-7 day boundary.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT SURVIVES, on capacity not dispatch: coal is retiring, so cheap gas can take share over time but expensive gas cannot reliably hand it back. 2022 is the counterexample of record: Henry Hub hit $6.60 and gas burn still ROSE >7% y/y because coal stockpiles were 65-76 days and rail could not replenish.
body.THE_WORKED_INSTANCE_IS_TVA_AND_WE_DO_NOT:
Greg's instance: 'a drought or flood conditions gets real expensive real fast for TVA because they have so much hydro gen.' TVA is the cleanest place in the country to see the inverted U - it is named for its dam system, carries a large hydro fleet, and is a serious gas burner, so when water goes to either tail the substitution shows up in TVA's gas burn fast and hard.

MEASURED S112: WE DO NOT SERVE TVA. grid_stack.bas carries CISO, ERCO, MISO, PJM, SOCO, SWPP and US48. Of the five Southeast BAs the S111 research named as the largest summer-burn region - SOCO, TVA, DUK, FPL, SCEG - we serve exactly ONE. For scale on what one is worth: SOCO alone is 6.3% of US48 generation at 49.7% GAS SHARE, the highest of any BA we carry. The four missing ones are comparably sized, sit in the highest-gas-share region in the country, and include the single BA where the hydro mechanism is most legible.

SO THE HYDRO GAP AND THE BA GAP ARE THE SAME GAP. Serving hydro at US48 level would average TVA's drought against the Pacific Northwest's runoff and show very little; the signal lives at the BA level, in a BA we do not have. Registry A-16 and A-18.

AND TVA IS FEDERAL, WHICH IS WHY THE DATA EXISTS TO BE HAD (Greg): 'their data should be published because they are a govt entity.' Verified - TVA is a corporate agency and instrumentality of the United States, created by Act of Congress in 1933, the largest government-owned electricity provider in the country. It publishes per dam: observed level, PREDICTED elevation, PLANNED GENERATION RELEASES in cfs updated through the day, and the year-long reservoir operating guide.

THAT IS THE INSTRUMENT THE INVERTED U NEEDS, AND IT IS FORWARD-DATED. Hydro output alone cannot carry a sign because the same low reading comes from flood spill and from drought drawdown. A planned release plus an operating guide states what the operator intends to run BEFORE it runs - which puts it in the one class the horizon research says survives past the 5-7 day weather boundary, beside the forward calendar and the nuclear refuelling schedule.

PUBLISHED IS NOT SERVED OVER AN API - said plainly so nobody banks it as done. No documented public TVA API surfaced when searched; the posted route is the Lake Levels pages and the Lake Info app, and tva.com returns 403 to an automated fetch, which is a scraping-policy fact and not an availability one. Cheapest first: USGS Water Data APIs (REST, machine-readable, real-time streamflow and gage height, national), then USACE - the agency Greg named as the one ordering the gates open - then TVA's own series, then FOIA.
body.THE_STATIONS_DO_NOT_SIT_WHERE_THE_LOAD_I:
GREG'S MAPPING, S112: SOCO = Atlanta. SCEG = Charleston. TVA = Nashville. FPL = Jacksonville or Miami, 'though they stretch up the east coast now'. DUK = Charlotte and Cincinnati, 'since it stretches out too'. Then the qualifier, applied to all five: 'just those cities probably is a bad representation anymore.'

MEASURED: nws_temp_feed.STATION_WEIGHTS_RAW is 16 hand-set metros, and ATL at 0.055 is the ONLY Southeast station in it. All five BAs Greg mapped resolve to that one station; four of the five have no station at all. The same file's own header calls the weights 'a documented FIRST CUT the agent tunes' (S88) - they were never tuned - and CLAUDE.md already carries the mirror hole: Ohio has no station at all against PJM being the largest gas-burning BA.

A BA IS NOT A COMPANY. EIA-930's DUK respondent is Duke Energy CAROLINAS; Duke's Ohio/Kentucky utility sits inside PJM. So Cincinnati is a PJM station, not a DUK one - and that is the Ohio hole, reached from the other direction. Verify respondent boundaries against EIA's BA list at build time, never from the company name: the Carolinas alone split across DUK, CPLE and CPLW.

WHY THE METROS WENT STALE, and it is a DRIFT not a constant (Greg): 'there's been so much growth in the South's suburbs that the major cities aren't really representative of where the majority of their loads are.' The airport ASOS sits at the old core; the residential cooling load that drives Southern summer gas burn moved to the suburbs and exurbs. A hand-set weight is therefore a DECAYING quantity - representative when set, less so every year, with nothing in the system reporting the decay. D23 in a new place: a fixed value standing in for a moving one.

THE FIX IS MEASUREMENT, AND IT HAS BEEN AVAILABLE SINCE S99 UNUSED. We hold each BA's OWN daily demand and its OWN day-ahead demand forecast (grid_stack.demand_mwh / demand_forecast_mwh). So station weights need not be argued from population - fit candidate stations' degree-days against the BA's realized demand and keep what explains it, per BA, never pooled.

AND IT RE-SCOPES WHAT A CITY IS FOR. For a BA we serve we do not need a city to infer today's load - EIA-930 reports it. The proxy earns its place only FORWARD, past the one day EIA gives. BA demand for the nowcast; stations for the forward driver; weights measured against the BA they claim to represent. Registry: A-19, paired with A-18 - four new BAs whose forward temperature signal is still Atlanta is not an improvement.

THE UNIT IS AN AGGREGATE OF SECONDARY CITIES (Greg): 'we'd have to aggregate places like Wilmington, NC and cities like that.' Wilmington is the case in miniature - coastal NC, inside CPLE, in no metro our 16-station set would ever reach, carrying a maritime profile Charlotte does not have.

AND WE DO NOT NEED A CONTACT, BECAUSE THE UTILITIES FILE IT. Greg: 'I used to know people at those places and would be able to ask them but I don't know if they're still there.' The weather-normalization method is disclosed in the Integrated Resource Plans filed with the state commissions. Duke's own IRP: the load models use a weighted average of temperatures from SEVERAL stations across the service territory, sites deliberately included in both states, against a 30-year normal RE-COMPUTED ANNUALLY. Public, dated, refiled - strictly better than a remembered phone number.

TWO THINGS FALL OUT. (1) A REBASE CADENCE: the industry re-computes normals yearly and NOAA rolls its 30-year Climate Normals each decade; our weights were set once at S88 and never revisited. Any set we land on carries a rebase date beside it or the decay Greg described just recurs. (2) THEIR LIST IS A PRIOR, NOT THE ANSWER: their set is tuned to retail SALES, ours has to explain the BA's GAS BURN. EIA-930 hands us the BA's own realized demand daily, so every candidate set is scoreable against the thing it claims to predict. Take the IRP list as a free expert candidate pool; keep what measures.

GREG NAMES THE TWO, AND THEY BROKE MY OWN BA LIST (S112): 'you have to pick up Raleigh and Wilmington in NC because so much of the South's electric load is in the suburbs or smaller metros.' Both are in CPLE - Duke Energy Progress East, about 100 plants and 64.7 TWh a year - a respondent A-18 had omitted because I wrote 'DUK' meaning 'Duke' one message after flagging that exact error for Cincinnati. The Carolinas are THREE respondents (DUK, CPLE, CPLW). Enumerate against EIA's BA reference table, never from memory of who owns what: a BA you never asked for reports nothing, so its absence is silent.

THE PAIR IS WELL CHOSEN. Raleigh is the Triangle - among the fastest-growing load centres in the country and invisible to any national top-16 metro list. Wilmington is coastal, and a cold-air damming or coastal-front day puts 15-20F between it and Charlotte. NC alone is mountain, Piedmont and coastal plain: one state, three temperature regimes, currently zero stations.

AND IT KILLS THE PRIMITIVE, not just the list. Ten Southeast stations cannot be APPENDED to a 16-station national weighted average - renormalise and every other region dilutes, do not and the South double-counts. The primitive must be PER-BA degree days, each BA with its own station set, with the national number DERIVED as a roll-up weighted by each BA's measured gas burn. EIA-930 supplies those weights, so the last hand-set number in the chain becomes a measured one.

WHY THE SOUTH IS THE SPECIAL CASE, beyond growth: the Southeast leads the country in heat-pump and electric-resistance heating, concentrated in the detached suburban stock Greg is describing. Southern stations therefore drive BOTH peaks through the electric meter - summer cooling and winter heating - where a Northeast station drives the winter peak through the gas meter. CONSEQUENCE FOR FORM: below a heat pump's balance point the resistance strips cut in, so Southern winter electric load is sharply CONVEX in the cold tail, not linear in HDD, and the jump is filled with gas. A linear degree-day term under-calls the Southern cold extreme by construction.
body.CAN_TVA_CARRY_THE_OTHERS_GREGS_HYPOTHESI:
THE CLAIM (Greg, S112): 'you could probably carry TVA's hydro levels across SOCO, SCEG and part of Duke percentage wise because their dams are along the same rivers... when TVA is curtailed so are those others.' Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS WITH A NAMED TEST, not as doctrine.

NOTE THE FORM, because it is the right one and it is not an accident. 'When TVA is curtailed so are those others' is a claim about a STATE co-occurring, not about levels correlating. That is exactly what D23/D28 says a condition must be written on, and it is the only form that survives the inverted U - a level cannot carry a sign when the same low reading comes from spill and from drawdown, but a CURTAILED state can, because curtailment is what both tails produce.

NOT THE SAME RIVERS - THE SAME HEADWATERS, which is the stronger version of the claim. TVA is the Tennessee basin, draining northwest to the Ohio. Alabama Power is Coosa, Tallapoosa and Black Warrior - 11 lakes, 14 plants - draining south to the Gulf. Georgia Power is Chattahoochee, Savannah, Oconee. Duke Carolinas is Catawba-Wateree and Keowee-Toxaway; SCEG is Saluda and Broad. Different rivers, different oceans. But the SOURCE REGION is one block: the southern Appalachian highlands of western NC, north Georgia, east Tennessee and upstate SC, the wettest ground in the eastern US, feeding TVA's tributary reservoirs and the headwaters of the Savannah, Catawba, Chattahoochee, Coosa and Broad alike. The same fronts, the same tropical remnants and the same droughts hit all of them. So what transfers is the REGIONAL WATER ANOMALY, not the operating state of any particular dam - and that is a better basis for a percentage carry than shared plumbing would have been.

THE WORKED INSTANCE IS 2007-2008 AND IT IS CLEAN. Second-driest year on record for the region, over a third of it in exceptional drought. Documented independently: low lake levels forced TVA AND Duke Energy in North Carolina to cut hydro and substitute fossil generation - Greg's claim, stated by an outside source, naming the substitution that lands on gas. In the same window Lake Lanier fell to 50% of storage in Georgia Power's state and Lake Norman sat less than a foot above the license minimum for Duke's McGuire nuclear plant. Three utilities, three basins, one water state.

AND THAT LAST DETAIL IS A SECOND MECHANISM, NOT COLOUR: a reservoir low enough to threaten a nuclear plant's cooling-water licence minimum takes down a stack LEVEL as well as a forcing. In the extreme drought tail the water anomaly hits hydro output AND nuclear availability, and both fill with gas. That links this to A-17 - the forward nuclear outage schedule is not the only way nuclear goes missing.

GREG'S DUKE EXCEPTION IS RIGHT, AND FOR A SHARPER REASON THAN STATED. Duke Carolinas' water IS Appalachian and DOES share the driver - Lake Norman in 2007 proves it. What excludes the rest of Duke is not hydrology but BA MEMBERSHIP: the Ohio/Kentucky/Indiana footprint is inside PJM and MISO, different respondents entirely, with essentially no hydro. So 'part of Duke' resolves to 'the DUK respondent, and check CPLE/CPLW' - the same company-is-not-a-BA correction A-19 makes from the temperature side, arriving independently from the water side.

THE ONE CONFOUNDER THAT WOULD BREAK A NAIVE CARRY - PUMPED STORAGE, and it is large. EIA-930 instructs that where a BA cannot separate pumped storage from conventional hydro, BOTH ARE REPORTED AS WAT. Pumped storage does not enter a water-curtailed state; it runs on price and load shape. Measured capacities: Duke's Bad Creek (1,065 MW, plus a 335 MW uprate) and Jocassee (710 MW) are about 2,200 MW of pumped storage - comparable to SOUTHERN COMPANY'S ENTIRE HYDRO FLEET of 2,730 MW across 34 facilities. SCEG's Fairfield is 587 MW against a small conventional fleet. TVA's Raccoon Mountain is about 1,700 MW against a large conventional one. So the WAT field means CATEGORICALLY DIFFERENT THINGS per BA: water-driven in TVA and SOCO, price-and-load-driven in DUK and probably SCEG. The confounder does not falsify the curtailment co-movement - it DILUTES it, by a factor that differs per BA, which is precisely how a 'percentage-wise' carry fitted on one BA would silently fail on another. Same field, different meaning per cell: the disease this desk keeps rediscovering.
CHECK AT BUILD: Rocky Mountain (1,095 MW pumped, Oglethorpe 75% / Georgia Power 25%) sits inside the SOCO footprint, and EIA-930 reports by BALANCING AUTHORITY not by ownership, so it likely lands in SOCO's WAT despite being mostly a co-op's. Georgia Power's Wallace Dam adds 321 MW.

THE TEST, and it needs no new feed once WAT is served: seven years of daily per-BA hydro sit in the store already (2019-2026, several droughts and several wet years). Define the curtailed STATE per BA off its own distribution, then measure P(SOCO curtailed | TVA curtailed) against the base rate, per season, per BA, never pooled. If it holds, the prize is HORIZON, not tidiness: TVA is the only one of the four that publishes FORWARD water - predicted elevation and planned releases - so a confirmed transfer turns TVA's forward reservoir guide into a forward hydro signal for three BAs that publish none. Registry A-20.

FALSIFIER: if the curtailment co-occurrence does not clear the base rate on the conventional-hydro component per BA and per season, the carry is refuted for that cell - and per D31 that refutation is SCOPED to the cell and the instrument, never generalised to 'Southeast hydro does not co-move'.
body.WHY_TVA_LEADS_THE_TESTIMONY_AND_THE_STRU:
THE TESTIMONY (Greg, S112, and he hedged it himself so it is recorded hedged): TVA is 'really heavy handed when it comes to hydro issues and just do what they want and the others downstream just have to deal with it... I do remember hearing that more than once from those guys and not as nicely as I stated it.' First-hand from utility people, recalled, repeated. Sentiment is not tradeable - but it is a POINTER, and this one points at something checkable.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT UNDER IT, VERIFIED: FERC DOES NOT REGULATE FEDERAL AGENCY DAMS. TVA operates its river system under the TVA Act of 1933 by its own board's decision. Every one of the others - Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Duke, Dominion/SCEG - runs its dams under a FERC HYDROPOWER LICENSE, among the 1,600-plus non-federal projects FERC administers, with prescribed guide curves, minimum flows and drought plans written into the licence articles (Georgia Power's Wallace Dam is FERC P-2413; Rocky Mountain and Catawba-Wateree have run public relicensings). Deviating means filing for a variance. So the asymmetry the operators complained about IS REAL AND IT IS STATUTORY: one party has discretion, four have paperwork.

WHY THAT UPGRADES THE CARRY HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN JUST COLOURING IT. Shared rainfall gives SYMMETRIC co-movement with no lead. Discretion-versus-licence gives an ASYMMETRIC, DIRECTIONAL, LEAD-LAG channel: TVA can move first and move fast; a licensee moves late, inside its guide, or after a filing. That converts 'TVA correlates with the others' into 'TVA LEADS the others', which is the difference between a redundant series and a forward signal. AND IT IS FALSIFIABLE IN A WAY THE SYMMETRIC VERSION IS NOT: if the mechanism is TVA's discretion, the lead-lag must be ASYMMETRIC - TVA to the others strong, the others to TVA weak. If both directions come back equally strong, it is common weather and nothing else, and TVA's forward data buys no horizon.

BE HONEST ABOUT 'DOWNSTREAM' - it is mostly not literal. TVA drains northwest to the Ohio; Alabama Power runs to the Gulf; Georgia Power, Duke and SCEG run to the Atlantic. Different rivers, different oceans. Three real propagation channels instead: (1) LITERAL, in north Georgia, where TVA's Nottely, Chatuge and Blue Ridge reservoirs physically sit in another state's territory - the classic friction point; (2) REGULATORY, the discretion asymmetry above, which makes TVA's response FASTER rather than physically upstream; (3) COMMERCIAL, and for a gas desk this is probably the biggest - TVA short on hydro buys and burns into the same regional power market the others sell into, so the water shock reaches them as PRICE and as tightness whoever's river it was.

AND CHANNEL (3) IS DIRECTLY MEASURABLE ONCE TVA IS SERVED: TVA's own gas_mwh in EIA-930 is the transmission channel itself. That is a second reason to do A-18 beyond hydro - serving TVA gets the BA where the water shock lands FIRST and the gas response it produces, in one row.

THE INVERSION WORTH CARRYING, because it cuts against what I said first. I called TVA the only one of the four publishing forward water. That is true of forward INTENT - and it is true BECAUSE TVA has discretion, so its intentions have to be published to be known. But the licensees publish something arguably better for forecasting: a BINDING RULE. A FERC licence article specifies target elevations by date, minimum flows, and a drought contingency plan, filed publicly and enforceable. Where TVA's future requires trusting a forecast, a licensee's future is partly a legal constraint. Both are forward-usable, by OPPOSITE mechanisms - discretion published as intent, constraint published as rule - and the licence route has never been looked at.
body.THE_DIVIDE_IS_THE_MECHANISM_AND_I_UNDERS:
I FRAMED THIS TOO WEAKLY FIRST TIME. I wrote 'not the same rivers - the same headwaters', which reads as a regional-weather correlation. Greg's version is tighter and it is literal: 'the same rain that hits Tennessee and north Georgia, big TVA areas, affects the rivers in SOCO territory, SCEG territory, Duke territory. TVA has dams in north Georgia and southern Tennessee.' Verified, and the geography is better than the claim needed.

TVA'S DAMS ARE PHYSICALLY IN GEORGIA. Blue Ridge and Nottely reservoirs plus part of Chatuge sit in north Georgia - over 11,000 acres and about 250 miles of shoreline. Blue Ridge is on the Toccoa, the uppermost of four TVA dams on the Toccoa/Ocoee. Nottely is in UNION COUNTY, built as a flood-storage structure to regulate flow at Hiwassee. Chatuge is in TOWNS COUNTY.

AND THE DIVIDE RUNS BETWEEN THE TWO UTILITIES' DAMS. The Etowah drains the SOUTH side of the Tennessee Valley Divide while the Toccoa drains the NORTH side - the Toccoa into TVA's Blue Ridge, the Etowah south to the Oostanaula at Rome and on into the Coosa, which is Alabama Power's Weiss, Neely Henry and Logan Martin. The Chattahoochee rises NEAR THE UNION/TOWNS COUNTY LINE - the same two counties that hold Nottely and Chatuge. Further east the Eastern Continental Divide separates the Gulf-flowing systems from the Savannah headwaters that feed Georgia Power's Tugalo and Tallulah and Duke's Keowee-Toxaway.

SO IT IS ONE STORM TOTAL, PARTITIONED BY A RIDGE. Rain falling on Fannin, Union, Towns, Lumpkin and Rabun counties loads TVA's reservoirs on the north side and SOCO's Coosa and Chattahoochee systems on the south side from the SAME EVENT. Same again on the NC escarpment - Transylvania, Jackson, Macon, Clay, Cherokee - where TVA's Fontana and Hiwassee sit against the Savannah and Broad/Saluda headwaters. This is not a correlation inherited from shared climate; it is the same precipitation measured on both sides of a divide.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT CHANGES THE TEST, and it is the valuable part: a shared CLIMATE driver produces co-movement on DROUGHT timescales - months - which is nearly useless to a desk working day-ahead to two weeks. A shared STORM driver produces co-movement on EVENT timescales - days to weeks - which is exactly our horizon. So A-20 must be run at event scale, not just seasonally, and the driver variable is basin precipitation and streamflow on the DIVIDE COUNTIES (USGS gauges, free and machine-readable), not a regional drought index.
THAT IS ALSO THE SHARPER FALSIFIER: if the co-movement appears only at seasonal scale and vanishes at event scale, the 'same rain' mechanism is NOT what is driving it, and the carry buys no tradeable horizon however good the seasonal correlation looks.

AND IT TURNS TVA FROM A CORRELATE INTO AN INSTRUMENT. TVA's north Georgia dams are STORAGE and FLOOD-CONTROL structures - Nottely exists to regulate flow at Hiwassee - so they capture the event and hold it, and TVA PUBLISHES their observed elevation, predicted elevation and planned releases. The same storm's loading of the Chattahoochee, Etowah and Savannah appears with far less public forward reporting. So TVA's published reservoir response is in effect A PUBLISHED GAUGE OF A STORM THAT ALSO LOADED THREE OTHER SYSTEMS. That is the concrete form of Greg's carry, and it is stronger than a fitted percentage: an instrument, not a coefficient.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN CAVEAT: I said 'downstream is mostly not literal'. Refine it. TVA's water does not flow to SOCO - the divide sends it the other way - but the LOADING is shared at the event, and TVA's dams sit inside Georgia, which is both the physical partition point and the political friction Greg's contacts were describing. Both things are true at once and they are the same geography.
body.AGGREGATION_IS_RIGHT_BUT_THE_CANCELLATIO:
GREG'S RULE (S112): 'you can probably aggregate those cities into CPL load. If it's really hot in Charlotte but Raleigh is getting rain all day, they will cancel to some degree.' Correct, and CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE - the aggregation is already done the right way and the reason needs recording so nobody 'simplifies' it later.

WHAT WE ALREADY DO RIGHT: nws_temp_feed.gas_weighted() computes HDD and CDD PER STATION and then weights the DEGREE DAYS. It does not average temperature and then take degree days. Same in _gas_weight_forecast. That order is not cosmetic.

WHY THE ORDER MATTERS, AND WHY 'CANCEL' IS ONLY PARTLY TRUE. Cooling load is CONVEX above the balance point, so by Jensen the mean of the degree days exceeds the degree days of the mean. Charlotte at 98 with Raleigh at 78 does NOT deliver the load of both at 88 - it delivers MORE. So dispersion ADDS load relative to what the footprint average suggests, and averaging temperature first would UNDER-CALL every high-dispersion day by construction. The cancellation Greg describes is real in direction and incomplete in size, and the asymmetry has a sign we can state in advance.

THE SAME ERROR STILL LIVES ON THE TIME AXIS - this is the open half. degree_days() takes a DAILY MEAN temperature, so a day running 60F overnight to 96F in the afternoon and a flat 78F day both score CDD 13 while drawing very different AC load, because the afternoon peak is what sets the burn. The convexity was handled across SPACE and is still collapsed across TIME. The raw hourly observations are already ingested (--ingest-hourly -> nws_hourly/), and the S90 record already called the daily degree-day store 'the same reduction mistake' - it is still what feeds gw_cdd.

AND RAIN CANCELS LESS THAN THE TEMPERATURE DROP IMPLIES, for two independent reasons Greg's own example runs straight into. (1) LATENT LOAD PERSISTS: Southern cooling load answers to wet bulb and dew point, not dry bulb alone - a rainy day is a humid day and the AC keeps pulling moisture out after the dry bulb falls. Our index is DRY BULB ONLY; dewpoint, wet_bulb and humidity appear ZERO times in this brain. (2) SOLAR OUTPUT FALLS: cloud and rain cut solar generation, which pushes load back onto gas. So rain is BEARISH gas through load and BULLISH gas through the solar residual, and both halves are measurable because solar_mwh is served.

AND THE PRECIP FIELD IS ALREADY THERE AND UNREAD. gas_weighted emits gw_precip, gas-weighted, every day. It appears exactly ONCE in this brain, as a bare name in a field list - zero plays, zero conditions. A-15 for the fourth time: the feed is built, the value is correct, nothing reads it. Greg's example is precisely the day it exists for. Registry A-21.

CORRECTED BY GREG, AND THE CORRECTION IS STRUCTURAL: 'it's not like both at 98 is my main point. They are 2 cities in the same utility. They won't burn gas independent of one another. CPL is an aggregate of the entire footprint.' I led with the Jensen arithmetic and put the convexity on the WRONG AXIS.

THE STRUCTURE FIRST. Charlotte and Raleigh are not two load centres each with its own gas burn. They are two SAMPLING POINTS inside one balancing footprint that dispatches as a single unit. There is no 'Charlotte's burn' and 'Raleigh's burn' - there is one dispatch against one aggregate load. So the stations are THERMOMETERS, NOT LOAD CENTRES, and the station problem is a MEASUREMENT problem - estimate the footprint's area-integrated weather from point samples - not a combination-of-independent-burns problem. Getting that backwards is what made me argue about whether two temperatures cancel, when they were never two separate things to cancel.

THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS STILL STANDS - per-station degree days, then weight, never average temperature first - but it is a MEASUREMENT convention, correct because load responds non-linearly to temperature at each point being sampled. It is not the main event, and it is demoted here to say so.

WHERE THE CONVEXITY THAT MATTERS ACTUALLY LIVES, and it is better posed than what I wrote: the footprint's GAS BURN is convex in the footprint's LOAD, because gas is the RESIDUAL and every cheaper term in the stack saturates - nuclear and coal are levels, wind and solar and hydro are forcings, so as load climbs an increasing share of each additional MWh lands on gas. That is the curve the desk actually needs, it is per-BA, and it is MEASURABLE TODAY from data we already hold: demand_mwh against gas_mwh, per respondent, back to 2019. We have never measured it.

AND THE NOWCAST NEEDS NO STATIONS AT ALL. EIA-930 reports the footprint's own demand, so for any BA we serve the aggregate load is MEASURED, not estimated from thermometers. The station set is the FORWARD instrument only - which is exactly the re-scoping A-19 already carries, arrived at here from the opposite direction.
body.WHAT_WE_ARE_ACTUALLY_SOLVING_FOR_AND_WHA:
THE SCOPING CALL (Greg, S112, now D35): 'we are trying to find overall gas demand. Don't care who is burning it or where.' Binding. NO per-BA number is ever a deliverable - no per-BA scoreboard, no play concluding 'SOCO drove it'. Per-BA is ARITHMETIC, not a goal.

AND IT IS ARITHMETIC WE CANNOT SKIP. (1) The stack is a per-BA SUBTRACTION - gas is load minus wind minus solar minus hydro minus nuclear minus coal, and that only means something inside the unit that actually balances. ERCOT's wind does not serve PJM's load, so a national 'load minus wind' is not a quantity at all. (2) The response is CONVEX, so the TOTAL IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM THE AVERAGE: a national CDD of 10 is either uniform mildness (low burn) or Texas at 20 against the Northwest at 0 (high burn). Greg's own cancellation rule is the proof - Charlotte hot and Raleigh rainy cancel TO SOME DEGREE, and it is exactly that incompleteness that forces you to compute the pieces and sum them. Decomposing is how you get an accurate TOTAL, not a detour from it.

THE STOPPING RULE IT GIVES US, which we did not have: add BAs until the served set RECONCILES TO US48 within tolerance, then stop. US48 is carried as its own EIA-930 respondent, so the ground truth is in hand and the gap is computable today. Not 'cover the map' - 'close the sum'.

AND THE TARGET IS NOT A NATIONAL AGGREGATE - Greg asked and the answer is no. Henry Hub is ONE PHYSICAL POINT: piping owned or leased by Sabine Pipe Line LLC near ERATH, LOUISIANA, roughly nine interstate plus three-to-four intrastate interconnects, with the NYMEX NG contract physically deliverable FOB at the buyer's interconnect. It is not an index of many points and it is not a generic national price. Every other region prices at a BASIS DIFFERENTIAL reflecting local conditions, transport cost and available transmission capacity.

SO THE OBJECT IS 'DEMAND HENRY HUB CAN SEE', NOT 'NATIONAL DEMAND'. New England load can spike Algonquin with little HH response, because the binding constraint there is pipe INTO the region rather than gas AT Henry. Gulf-coast LNG feedgas is the most HH-coupled demand there is - which makes lng_feedgas_bcfd sitting null and 278 days stale a larger hole than its size suggests. BANKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the Southeast BAs this session argued for sit on the Gulf corridor and are among the better-transmitting ones, so that work is aimed at the target rather than incidental to it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROLL-UP: weight the national number by gas burn TIMES HH TRANSMISSION, not by burn alone - and MEASURE the transmission by regressing HH day-moves on per-BA burn changes, never assert it off a pipeline map. That is the one weight in the chain still unmeasured.
